**Why Christ was a priest by an oath. Chapter IX.**

[Marginal note: Paul] **H**Our Paul, educated at the feet of Gamaliel and instructed in the third heaven, did not keep silent about how Christ was constituted a priest by an oath, saying to the Hebrews: "Other priests indeed were made without an oath, but he with an oath by him who said [Marginal note: David] to him: 'The Lord has sworn and will not change his mind, "You are a priest forever."'" But what this oath implies, and how it binds all who swear so that they cannot depart from the oath without cause, this mystery is hidden. The more recondite Hebrews say that an oath connects many things, especially that exalted septenary (sevenfold principle) from which all things proceed, just as the words for 'oath' and 'septenary' are the same in their language, so much so that השבע (hasbah), which means 'he swore,' comes from שבע (sheva), which means 'seven,' so that according to their understanding, 'He swore' means 'he sevened,' or 'he attested by seven,' and brought those seven as witnesses: Wishing to signify this, Abraham, when he made a covenant with Abimelech, set seven ewe-lambs as a testimony; through these seven ewe-lambs he intended to represent that exalted septenary, according to which stand the seven spirits who are in the presence of the throne of God. Hence, the transgression of an oath is, in a way, to wish to make those witnesses false...

--- Page 600 ---
TONE THREE. 230

false witnesses, and to deprive themselves of the influence of those, from whom comes all good. Therefore the Lord swore to Christ, appealing to Him through that septenary, and communicating to Him His septenary influence in every way, according to that oracle of Isaiah, in which concerning Christ made a pri- [Marginal note: Isaias] est by this oath it says: "A shoot will come out from the root of Jesse, and a flower from his root will ascend, and the Spirit of the Lord will rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom, and understanding, the spirit of counsel, and might, the spirit of knowledge, and piety: and the spirit of the fear of the Lord will rest upon him:" As if it were said, according to that septenary, the spirit of understanding will rest in him, and the remitter of faults: Also grace or piety, justice & terror, beauty & rectitude, victory & perpetuity, splendor & adornment, life & kingdom, so that not without cause he might say: [Marginal note: CHRIST. Origen.] "All things the Father gave to me." Which Origen, pondering, writing on that passage of Isaiah, [Marginal note: Isaias] "Seven women will take hold of one man," says: "The Holy Spirit with his gifts was upon many, but rested on none, except on JESUS: who is that unique bridegroom, whom the seven women, that is, that exalted septenary, apprehended with an indissoluble bond:" For the spirit of wisdom came with other gifts, upon Moses, but did not rest, [Marginal note: Moses.] especially when he erred in striking the rock, because of which the leadership of the people to the promised land was taken from him: It came upon Aaron, but in the sin of the [Marginal note: Aaron.] calf it departed: It came also upon Isaiah, but what did he say? [Marginal note: Isaias.] "I am a man of unclean lips:" It came also upon David, but feeling he had deserved that by which he would rightly be deprived, [Marginal note: David] he cried saying: "Do not take your Holy Spirit from me." And since there is no one who does not sin, there is no one from whom the spirit of the Lord does not depart for a time, except Jesus alone, of whom it was said to John: "Upon whom you see the Spirit descending, and remaining on him, this is the Son of God, this is he who baptizes with the Holy Spirit, powerful to impart that very Spirit, which he firmly possesses, to others:" And because I saw (said [Marginal note: John.] John) the Spirit descending, and remaining, I bore witness, that this is the Son of God. Therefore the spirit remained, and that exalted septenary remained firmly upon Jesus, and without any interruption, and without any departure: But why this? Because the Lord swore, and will not repent: He swore, that he would be a priest forever: He swore, that he would be the High Priest: He swore, that he would be holy, pure, clean, and separated from sinners, so that he could take away the sins of all. And because he swore, therefore the spirit rested upon him, and that which is greater than all, which the Father gave to him: Whence that third thing is equated, namely שבת Sabat, which the [Marginal note: Hebrews.] Hebrews say agrees with the oath and the septenary: and signifies rest. Therefore the sevenfold spirit rested in him and that exalted septenary, because the almighty Father swore to him, that always remaining holy and divine, he would sanctify others, and make them divine.

How he was a priest according to the order of Melchizedek. Chapter X.
[Decorative initial V] By oath he constituted our Christ the High Priest, he established him according to the order of Melchizedek: Which since it is known to all, let us see therefore what is the order of Melchizedek, according to which Christ was constituted. Therefore, having discussed those things which in Genesis [Marginal note: Genesis.]

Four are touched upon by Paul, of which the first is: because Melchizedek is introduced in scripture without father and mother, having neither beginning of days nor end, thus the Son of God was constituted priest without beginning and without end of days, since he is eternal; nor in

[Marginal note: Rabbi Solomon, Hebrews] was made like the Son of God. However, Rabbi Solomon says, and with him many wise men
[Marginal note: Jerome, Shem] of the Hebrews, to whom Jerome assents, that Melchizedek is an appellative name, and signifies a just king, whose proper name is Shem: he, of course, the son of Noah: and thus we have his father, although not expressly from scripture: Thus also our Christ has a father, although not expressed, where his priesthood is discussed.

The second is, because he was king of Salem, that is, of peace, signifying our Christ as High Priest and king of true peace: who came to give and leave that true peace to us: which the world cannot give: Therefore, as he entered the world, his ministers sang: And on earth peace to men of good will: And leaving the world,
[Marginal note: CHRIST.] he himself said to his disciples: My peace I give to you, my peace I leave to you; not as the world gives, do I give to you.

The third is the interpretation of the name, which is
[Marginal note: Isaiah] king of righteousness, fitting with our Christ, concerning whom Isaiah says: And a king shall reign, and he shall be wise: and he shall execute judgment and righteousness in the earth.

The fourth, which is inferred from this, is that just as Melchizedek was king and priest, so also is Christ: Who therefore came from the royal tribe of Judah, so that he might assume the kingdom by hereditary right according to the flesh, just as he had also received it from the heavenly Father, which he would also give to us together with the priesthood.
[Marginal note: John] Hence John in the Apocalypse: And he made us a kingdom and priests to God and his Father:
[Marginal note: Peter] With whom Peter, writing to the scattered strangers in Pontus, and Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia, said: You are a chosen race, a royal priesthood.

The fifth, which I weigh more heavily, is the offering, which is reported to have been made by Melchizedek himself in bread alone and wine, no mention being made of animals or any other things whatsoever: Indeed, a rite most fitting for our High Priest Christ Jesus, who concluded every sacrifice in bread alone and wine, as in the primary substance of human food: To this sacrifice, all blood and the killing of animals, and whatever else was offered in the law, yielded: since now we do not need blood in which to be cleansed: because now in the blood of Christ the human race has been perfectly cleansed: and all things that were then unclean: because our law is of grace and watery, whence we no longer enter into this law or into the Christian family through the blood of circumcision, but through the water of baptism, then also, because nothing more expressly figures the mystical body of the universal church, of which Christ is the head, than bread: For this is made from many grains, and is the common and universal food of all nations: just as this mystical body is made up of many individuals of every nation that is under heaven. Hence this congregation is called the Catholic Church, that is, universal. And nothing more consonant with life than Chri

**TONUS TERTIUS.** [Page number] **231**

Christ came to give us that blood in which life most especially resides, as many wise men affirm and as we can clearly infer from sacred scripture. This, therefore, is the order of Melchisedech, in which our Christ was constituted priest and High Priest. And to him, as to the High Priest, Abraham gave, giving tithes of all things, and receiving a blessing from him. From which it is concluded that Melchisedech was greater than Abraham, by the argument of Paul, who says: [Marginal note: Paul] Without any contradiction, the lesser is blessed by the better. Since therefore he received tithes from Abraham, and consequently from Levi: who still (says [Marginal note: The same] Paul) was in his loins, and blessed him, he was greater than Abraham and Levi: and his priesthood greater than the Levitical and legal priesthood: this especially (as the [Marginal note: The same] Apostle weighs) because the legal priesthood ought to be transferred into that of Melchisedech, that is, into the priesthood of Christ, who was constituted priest according to the order of Melchisedech: Therefore Christ himself was not of the priesthood of Aaron, nor of the tribe of Levi, but of the royal tribe of Judah: so that it may be understood that the priesthood of Christ was royal, and according to the true order of a just king: Hence this declaration, "You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchisedech," was indeed a repudiation of the former commandment and priesthood, as weak and useless, since the law leads to no perfection. Therefore the priest who was made according to the law of a carnal commandment ought to cease, and he who was according to the power of an indissoluble life ought to arise: These things we have deduced from Paul. But why was Christ's eternal priesthood prefigured in the priesthood of Melchisedech? Responding to this, I will say with [Marginal note: Jerome] Jerome: If the vessel of election is amazed at the mystery, and confesses as ineffable that about which he disputes, how much more ought we, mere worms and gnats, to confess only the knowledge of our ignorance, and to have seen a most spacious house as if through a small hole? For great is the discourse, and interpretable to say, why Melchisedech was introduced without genealogy. And if the Hebrews truly say that he was Shem, what does this name Shem import, which translated into Latin signifies "name"? Perhaps that name which is above every name, just as when "virgin" is said, the Virgin who is above all virgins is understood: And the Apostle above all Apostles: and the Father above all fathers, and to conclude briefly from all things, in Melchisedech there was something divine and permanent, in which the eternal priesthood of Christ was represented: concerning which (as [Marginal note: Paul] Paul says) it is not lawful to speak, therefore let us come to other things.

**How much greater and better a priest Christ was than Aaron, and**
**all legal priests. Chapter XI.**

calves, but through his own blood he entered once into the holy places, having found eternal redemption. Six points are touched upon by Paul, in which Christ was a more perfect and excellent high priest than the legal and figurative one: First, because they obtained propitiation from God, by which, being appeased, He would favor them with temporal goods, as is clear in the whole promise of the law, by which it is said: If you obey me, you shall eat the good things of the land: And your seed shall possess the gates of their enemies: And one of you shall put to flight a thousand, and two, ten thousand, and such like: All of which were temporal, although they were a figure of eternal things. To which things, wiser men sometimes entered speaking of the future age, of blessed life, and of the true paradise of delights: To whose state one did not arrive through sacrifice, but through a better lot, and the precious death of the saints, as it had come to the prophet. But let us speak of sacrifice, by which only some sins were expiated, and not all: Hence, those purified by them did not deserve eternal reward, but those things which were promised according to the present age.
[Marginal note: Paul] But our High Priest was made (says Paul) of future good things, therefore through something greater and more perfect. Secondly, the Levitical priest entered a tabernacle made by hand, indeed, wooden, afterwards stone when the temple was erected: But our High Priest entered a tabernacle not made by hand, that is, not of this creation: By which tabernacle Origen understands heaven: Which could be confirmed by the testimony of Paul saying: We have a great High Priest, who has passed through the heavens, Jesus the Son of God: And again: We have such a high priest, who is seated at the right hand of the throne of majesty in the heavens, a minister of the sanctuary, and of the true tabernacle, which God pitched, and not man. But Origen himself strengthens his saying with the
[Marginal note: David] testimony of the divine Harper (David) saying: I remembered these things, and poured out my soul within me: for I will go into the place of the wonderful tabernacle, even to the house of God: And again in another psalm: Lord, who shall dwell in thy tabernacle, or who shall rest in thy holy mountain? He who walks without blemish, and works justice. And what is the place of the wonderful tabernacle, from which one arrives even to the house of God? And what is that tabernacle, of which the prophet, having become mindful, had his soul poured out within him, as if dissolved by some intolerable desire? Indeed, it was not that (tabernacle) made of goat skins, and curtains of fine linen, purple, hyacinth, and scarlet: Nor that which was captured by the Philistines: Nor that which was to be built by the son: But the Father's tabernacle, which, divided into many mansions, is
[Marginal note: CHRIST.] named in the plural by Christ saying: Make to yourselves friends of the mammon of iniquity, that when you shall fail, they may receive you into everlasting tabernacles. And by the Royal prophet in a psalm: How lovely are thy tabernacles, O Lord of hosts! My soul longs and faints for the courts of the Lord. This tabernacle, therefore, not made by hand, is heaven, which was made not by the hand of men, but by the power and command of God. There is also another tabernacle, in which God delights to dwell, which is called the temple of God by Paul saying: The temple of God, which you are. Therefore, the soul of each one, cleansed and purified, is the temple and tabernacle of God: And this not made by hand,

Thirdly, because the legal high priest entered into the holy places with the blood of goats, calves, rams, lambs, sparrows, and doves, or with the sprinkled ashes of a heifer, and such like: All these are animals, and pertain to cleansing the animal man: But Christ entered into the holy places through his own blood, so that he might cleanse all things so much better, inasmuch as the blood, I will not say of a man, but of the most holy Son of God, is more precious than the blood of animals, by which the animal man was cleansed: And consequently, so much more perfect is the priesthood of Christ cleansing in his own blood, than the legal priesthood cleansing in the blood of animals. But why almost all things (as the Apostle says) are cleansed in blood (he says "almost", because vessels of metals were purified by fire, and other vessels and garments were cleansed by water, as we read in the book of Numbers), I believe this is the reason: because sin draws its origin from blood and flesh, therefore expiation had to be made by blood: For the tribunal of God's justice, seeking punishment where sin was, wills that blood be shed, and the flesh, which were the fuel of sin, be suppressed: But in the legal and figurative sacrifice, which did not fully expiate, purifications were made in the figurative blood of animals. But Christ, coming, promising, and giving heavenly things, having become the head of all members of this mystical body, shed blood not human and subject to sin, and not of animals, but also most precious above all bloods that were in this mystical body, for the expiation of all. Hence our
[Marginal note: Paulus] Paul says: It was necessary that the copies of the heavenly things should be purified with those sacrifices of animals: but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these, that is, with the blood of the Redeemer, as
[Marginal note: Ioan.] John says in his epistle: The blood of Jesus Christ cleansed us from all sin: And
[Marginal note: Apocal.] in the Apocalypse: Who loved us, and washed us from our sins in his own blood: And now it is known to all that Christ, suffering, not in the figurative blood of animals, but in his own blood, satisfied the tribunal of divine justice.

Fourthly, because the legal priests, as often as they wished to obtain propitiation for sins recurring to them, entered into the holy places and sacrificed animals: But our High Priest Christ entered into the holy places once: because he ascended the cross once, offering himself to God the Father, and making satisfaction for all, not with a figurative, but with a true satisfaction, even for the preceding fathers: Because this offering to be made was already accepted by the Father before the foundation of the world, and in it were expiated as many as were saved: as
[Marginal note: Ioan.] John expressly says in the Apocalypse: All worshipped the beast, whose names are not written in the book of life of the Lamb, who was slain from the origin of the world. And
[Marginal note: Petrus] Peter: You were not redeemed with corruptible gold and silver from your vain conversation of paternal tradition, but with the precious blood, as of an immaculate and unblemished lamb, Christ, indeed foreknown before the foundation of the world, but manifested in the last times. Christ was the true victim, and every kind of sacrifice, and offering. Chapter XII.

[Decorative initial O] ffered therefore for us, he became a true victim, a burnt offering, a sacrifice, a sin offering, a guilt offering, a *cherbona* of peace offerings, that is, an oblation, a gift, and whatever was offered in the Law. For a *hostia* and a *victima* is that which is offered (as the authors of our language teach) when one attacks enemies or reports a victory or triumph over them: as the most skilled
[Marginal note: Ovid.] Poet in such matters sings: "The victim that fell by the conquering right hand is called a *victima*: from conquered enemies, it has the name *hostia*." Therefore, Christ, having attacked the enemy of the human race, offered Himself to the Father as a living *hostia*, and, conquering and subduing him, sacrificed Himself as a *victima*, so that He might at once report victory and offer Himself as a *hostia* from the subdued enemies:
[Marginal note: Paul] Therefore Paul says to the Ephesians: "Christ loved us and gave Himself up for us as an offering and a sacrifice to God for a fragrant aroma, so that He might rescue us from their hands, the enemies having been subdued."
[Marginal note: The same] And again he says to the Hebrews: "But now once at the consummation of the ages, he has appeared for the destruction of sin by his sacrifice."
[Marginal note: Origen.] Concerning which sacrifice Origen discusses many things in his epistle to the Romans. Christ was also a burnt offering (*holocaustum*), which among the Latins signifies "wholly consumed by fire": but in Hebrew it is called עולה habolah, which properly interpreted means "ascending": For he was wholly consumed by the fire of love, and consumed, and transformed into a spiritual nature. Hence, demonstrating what he was to be like, he was transfigured before them, his passible, obscure, and heavy body changed into an agile, luminous, and impassible body: But it did not remain so, because he was not yet truly consumed and transformed, having been offered as a burnt offering: But after the burnt offering was made on the cross, raising himself, he showed himself (as he was) completely transformed, entering through closed doors, appearing when he wished, and concealing himself at will: and finally, having become most light, he ascended gloriously in the sight of many: From which he was appropriately called עולה holah, that is, "ascending." Therefore, consumed, and by the power of divine fire transformed into the nature of fire itself, and spirit—

--- Page 608 ---
TONVS TERTIVS. 234

changed, he ascended to the Father, having first given the disciples faith concerning the truth of his resurrection for forty days: And ascending on high, he wished to take very many with him, according to that of the prophet: "Ascending on high, he led captivity captive." [Marginal note: David]

There was also a sacrifice offered for sin, which the Hebrews call חטאת (hatat), and properly interpreting, we can say nothing more fitting than 'peccatarium' (sin-offering) from חטאת (hata), which is 'sin': Concerning which sacrifice, Paul says to the Corinthians: [Marginal note: Paul] "He who knew no sin, made himself a sin-offering for us": for which faulty codices have, "he made sin for us": For how could he who knew no sin, make sin? And what fruit would he have brought us by making sin? Nor does that explanation given by some please: "he made sin", that is, "he offered himself for sin": because even if they agree in meaning, nevertheless that interpretation cannot be fitting.

Therefore, it was a 'peccatarium' (sin-offering), that is, offered for the sins of all. There was also a 'culpatarium' (guilt-offering), namely a sacrifice offered for guilt, or for error, to speak properly: Which sacrifice in the law is called אשם (asham): which we have translated as 'for trespass': In which, by the priest, or the anointed one sinning, and by the multitude, a calf was offered; but by the prince, a male goat: But a common person offered a female goat, or a sheep, as we read in Leviticus: [Marginal note: Leviticus] And with blood, partly sprinkled on the horn of the altar by the priest's finger, partly poured out at its base: All these things are full of mysteries: For by the calf, the male goat, and the female goat, the tribunal of divine justice was appeased, to which all those things correspond: which also signify that part in man in which is the fuel of sin, so that not without cause those who are to receive judgment and God's punitive justice are compared by the Savior to goats, who are of the caprine and hircine kind: Through which slain and sacrificed animals, God was easily appeased, with error being partly excused: And the horn of the altar, erected before that very tribunal, was sprinkled with the blood of the offered animal itself to appease the heavenly powers, which demand blood from those who sin according to the flesh and blood, so that according to the rectitude of justice, each one might be punished by those things through which he also sinned. And this was done by the finger of the priest, who intervened as a mediator to appease God with sinful man.

But Christ, having become not only Priest and High Priest, but also a male goat, a calf, a sheep, a lamb, and every kind of sacrifice, as we shall immediately declare, himself pouring out his own blood on every horn of the altar of the cross, more amply and perfectly appeased the Eternal Father and the tribunal of his justice, than was done by the blood of animals.

Nor is the blood that was poured out at the base of the altar, in much greater quantity than that with which the horn of the altar was sprinkled, devoid of mystery: because much more is the blood and merit acquired through the shed blood, which superabounds and is reserved, than that blood or merit applied to the horn of the altar by the finger of the true priest for the purification of the sinner: For the blood of Christ and his merit would have sufficed, and suffices, for thousands and tens of thousands of worlds, as our Theologians say. Therefore, the part that superabounds and is reserved is greater than that which is applied for our actual purification. But this also must be noted, GG ij

Therefore, the gods of those serving sin are either the belly, according to that saying of Paul: "Whose God is their belly": Or avarice, which is idolatry: [Marginal note: Paulus] Or the devil, whom those serving sin obey: All these things God will judge, as the Apostle says: "Food for the belly, and the belly for food, and God will destroy both it and them together with their instigator." And such is the difference between those serving God and those serving sin, as was between the children of Israel and the Egyptians: because, namely, their houses were smeared with the blood of the lamb: For the servants, indeed friends of God, and those who are justified from sin, ought to have their doorposts smeared with the blood of the Lamb, who takes away the sins of the world: by which they may deserve protection from the striking angel, grace for good works, and entrance to the heavenly kingdom: But those serving sin, deprived of that blood, the true protection of all, are killed by the striking angel, since he does not see in them the pledge of reconciliation: therefore they feel both their firstborn and all their strength crushed, and finally themselves suffocated in the sea, and utterly destroyed.

On the rod of Moses, and the cross. Chapter 14.

[Decorative initial V containing two figures] Beyond the typical lamb, in that passage of the Israelite people, there was present the sacramental rod, first very prodigious in the sight of Pharaoh, then very remarkable in all the miracles performed in the sea, the desert, and all places, until the people entered the land of promise: Which rod, although it was called Moses', was nevertheless, beyond all doubt, the power of God: upon which Moses was sustained, trusting in no power of his own. And among other things, this remarkable wonder was performed under the auspices of that rod, that when thrown on the ground, it turned into a serpent: When its tail was grasped by the one who threw it, it again appeared as a rod: From which we are taught that when the power of God is cast aside, one does not act except by the favor of the serpent, who, as the author of deceptions, very easily substitutes himself for the rod, favoring deceptions, since he cannot concur with true miracles. To the outcome of these deceptions, which is always evil, the wise person ought to look, so that, despising them and their author, he may adhere to the true worker, God: Therefore, Moses was commanded to grasp it by the tail, that is, to attend to the end and outcome of poisonous and deadly deceptions, and, driving them away, to rely solely on God: Which also indicate the removal of shoes from the feet, and the pasturing of flocks after the desert: For God had commanded him to remove the shoes from the feet of his affections, which he had shod with Egyptian doctrines: because the place and land, or state, to which he had come, was holy. For he no longer tarried in a desert place devoid of divine influences, but after the desert of magic and Egyptian art: For which we have it wrong; "to the inner parts of the desert": For he was not then dwelling in the inner recesses of the desert, but after the desert itself, namely in fertile Arabia, on Mount Sinai, irrigated by much divine influence: For on the summit of that mountain, which is called Horeb, God spoke intimately with Elijah: And on another peak of the same mountain, named Sinai, Moses...

--- Page 615 ---
CANTICI SECVNDI

if he gave the law, dealing with him most familiarly, and showing many wonders, so that it was not a desert, but a most irrigated place. Which rod, moreover, of divine power, when cast before Pharaoh, appeared as a serpent, especially to him and his wise men accustomed to magical arts: who performed all their illusions by the power of the ancient serpent. Hence, believing that Moses' power proceeded from the ancient serpent itself, they opposed him with forces which they had truly received from the evil serpent, and these were turned into serpents: But Moses' rod, that is, true divine power, although it appeared as a serpent, devoured those rods and necromantic powers: so that it might be indicated that the rod, that is, divine power, which overcomes all demonic force, performed miracles in Egypt, the Red Sea, and the desert. More fortunately, however, the true and universal redeemer Christ performed sublimer and more excellent wonders with the rod of the cross than the legislator Moses: since this power of Christ was not only a rod content with a single extension, but also, passing transversely, formed a strong and ample texture, as it were, from warp and weft. For the rod of Jacob and Moses was erected only upwards, but this rod of Christ was extended in every direction, in length, breadth, height, and depth: Therefore, it prevailed not only for the liberation of the single Israelite people, but for the whole human race and the aerial powers, conquering the latter and sustaining the former, so that nothing [marginal note: Paul] remained over which its power did not prevail. And of this the Apostle speaks, saying: "That you may be able to comprehend with all the saints what is the breadth, and length, and height, and depth," namely, of the supereminent knowledge of the charity and power of Christ affixed to the cross: Whose extension and intensity are indicated by the branches and their angles: For the branches are extended upwards, and downwards, and transversely, so that, stretched out into diverse and all parts of the world, they may signify that power diffused everywhere. Sixteen angles, namely four at each end of the shaft, indicate how intense its power is: For sixteen is the first number increased from the first growing twelve, and by which (as we said above) all growing things are distributed. But it must also be observed that one quaternary (group of four) is hidden in the earth, with the shaft fixed in the earth itself, or in stone: and twelve open angles appear in the three spreading branches: Which number twelve, arising through three led by four, or through four multiplied by three, of which the former (three) is divine and the latter (four) is elemental, expressly indicates that all divine and earthly things are reconciled in the cross itself, since in the twelve one is led by the other, and both are connected in it. And this is what the Apostle [marginal note: Paul] says: "It pleased [namely, the Father] that all fullness should dwell in him, and through him to reconcile all things, making peace by the blood of his cross, whether things on earth or things in heaven." Thus also in heaven, by this divided twelve, spiritual and corporeal things are reconciled, with intelligences assisting there, flowing through those twelve corporeal signs. The hidden quaternary of increase, however, signifies the fruit of the cross itself, hidden from our senses and judgments, but nevertheless that which is the root and foun-

TONVS TERTIVS.                                                                    238

...dation of all fruits and merits, just as the quaternary is the root of all
numbers. That duodenary also, is led by another no small mystery, namely, from
the four heads of the cross itself, three nails, and five wounds of him
suffering in it: Where the duodenary itself results from the material quaternary, the divine
ternary, and the conglutinative quinarius: For this is denoted among the Hebrews by the letter
ה, in which they say the world was fabricated and conglutinated, and which is the seal of that
craftsman spirit, which is called *nexus*. And this cross was once seen as a serpent,
not indeed deceptive and deadly, but salutary: concerning which it is said: Just as Moses [Marginal note: CHRIST]
exalted the serpent in the desert, so must the Son of Man be exalted, on the cross:
that is, extended in the manner of a cross, so that he himself was crucified, a cross, and
a serpent, exposed not for destruction, but for salvation, whence it follows: That everyone who
believes in him may not perish, but have eternal life. For just as the flesh of a serpent
brings healing to a poisonous wound, whence theriac is made, which is an antidote to poison,
from the flesh of the *thiri*, so the flesh of Christ provides health and life to all whom [Marginal note: The same]
not Christ himself bit, but the evil serpent: Therefore, against the poisons of this [serpent], that very
flesh must be eaten by us. And because he himself seemed to himself a wounded, leprous, and
spotted serpent, therefore he began to fear, to be weary, and to be sorrowful, and finally to say:
Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from me. For he was, and knew it was possible,
whence that "if" can be taken for "because" (as they say): For he greatly desired (if I am not mistaken)
another, more useful order of helping us: Nor, failing in supreme charity, did he condescend to the sensitive
part, as some suppose, since he was always ready to expose body and soul for his sheep:
But he was content to draw out a longer stay with us, so that he might perfect a more excellent work.
Hence he did not say that the cup should be removed, but that it should pass, and be deferred
until that time when he would fulfill that which the Apostle, conscious of these sacraments, says: [Marginal note: Paul]
"But last of all, the enemy, death, will be destroyed," that is, the angel of death, as he explains more clearly elsewhere, saying:
"That through death he might destroy him who had the power of death, that is, the devil:
and deliver those who through fear of death were all their lives subject to servitude."
However, the Father did not wish to acquiesce, not indeed despising the prayer of the supplicant, whom
he always heard, but so that all things might be weighed by their own weights, and distributed
at their own times and moments, which the Father himself holds in his power with a great
sacrament, so that it is not for us or the Apostles to know these things: But what he did not
perfect in the first advent, he will perfect in the second without any doubt. But to return to where
we digressed, although he felt horror from the terrifying passion and death offered,
nevertheless, grasping it by the tail, that is, looking towards the glorious end,
it again appeared as a distinguished and very famous rod: Which again appeared as a serpent
to the Pharisees and malicious ones who said: [Marginal note: Pharisees] "He casts out demons by Beelzebub, the prince of demons."
But he showed that divine power which would devour all diabolical force, proving that a demon
is cast out not by a demon, but by the finger and power of God. By which power, in many miracles in the Egypt of this world, he performed—

--- Page 617 ---
**SECOND CANTICLE**

...performed, in granted healings, in raising the dead, by multiplied bread, water changed into wine, and countless things of this kind, not for the destruction of the Egyptians, but always for benefit and advantage. Finally, he sanctified the sea, that is, the water of baptism, through which passage is given to us to divine fellowship on Sinai, where we hear the law and feel God acting intimately, and we are fed with better bread than that dew-like (manna), which indeed descended living from heaven, offered and baked in the oven of the cross. By which, finally, our teacher Christ introduced us into the true promised land, flowing with true milk and honey. Which Moses could not do, for he could not introduce the people to the figurative land with that rod, which he had misused by striking where and when he ought not. Therefore, we must rely more happily on the rod of the cross and Christ, than on Moses and Jacob, because relying on them, we will either fail on the way, or arrive only at a shadowy land, but supported by this, we will reach the land and the true dwellings of the living, following the leader who cannot err.
[Marginal note: Jacob]
Hence, when Jacob uttered his last words, by which he summarily foretold almost all the affairs of both the figurative and the true family, he no longer leaned on his staff, with which he crossed the Jordan, but leaned on this better rod, in whose power he foresaw all those things to be accomplished. For it is said in the text: "And he gathered his feet," that is, his affections, אל המטה (El hamitah): Which, although we have it well translated as "to the bed," can also be understood as "to the rod," for המטה (hamitah) signifies both "rod" and "bed" by changing the vowel points. Therefore, in the literal sense, "to the bed," but in the allegorical sense, it is more aptly transferred to the rod, which is the cross, whose power he foresaw no less than some of the ancients who venerated the sign of the cross before Christ, as men of no small authority write. Which was either by nature, or by the dictation of the spirit, or by wiser men more intelligently teaching what they did not know, how great things were to be done through the cross.

To what end sacrifices, and why chosen goats were commanded to be offered for sin. Chapter XV.

[Large decorative initial C containing a figure of a man] WHEN God came to institute sacrifices, he commanded many things to be offered for diverse and various expiations. Which indeed at first glance seems harsh and strange, namely, that God delights in the spilled blood of animals, in roasted or burned flesh, and in the aromas of these and other things, as it is said in many places: "And the Lord smelled a sweet savor." Therefore, these are held among the greatest sacraments. For some explanation of which, it must be firmly held that the supreme God is delighted by no odors, no flavors, nor is he fed by material foods from the flesh of animals, or by prepared breads, and smeared with oil, or drenched with some fat, although all these things were commanded to be done in the law. And this, either as a sacrament of those things which truly ought to be done by Christ, and of those things which consequently are to be performed by us, namely, by mortifying, according to the apostolic precept,
[Marginal note: Paul]
our members, and by offering as an acceptable sacrifice those things which are in us, of which

[Marginal note: Leviticus]
Which we read as prefigured with great mystery in Leviticus, where God commanded that two goats be chosen, and that a lot having been cast upon them, one should be sacrificed to God, but the other should be sent away into the desert to Azazel, the prince of all deserters. This goat, he-goat, or buck destined for Azazel is called "emissarius" in our translation, not indeed because it is given like a horse for impregnating females, but perhaps, although less appropriately, it is called emissarius because it was sent out. And this goat, before it was sent into the wilderness, was placed alive before the Lord, so that prayers first having been poured out over it, it might be sent into solitude to the accuser of the human race, so that the mouth of the accuser himself might be shut.

And so that we may reveal something of the sacrament enclosed here, that animal which was sent is called שעיר sabir in the Hebrew idiom, which means goat, kid, hairy, devil

**SECOND CANTICLE**

He made it, who was priest and victim, Christ Jesus, to God the eternal Father: Which he also commanded us to remember in his memory, although it was made once for the fullest remission of all sins: And this revocation of the offering, which was made to Azazel, or to any power of this kind, Moses (at God's command) [Marginal note: Moses.] foretold after thirty-three texts, in the manner of the Hebrews, which they call *passuchim*, hinting that after thirty-three years of the Messiah's life, this revocation ought to take place: For he says: "And they shall no longer sacrifice the sacrifice of Saharim, after whom they have prostituted themselves," having indeed so condescended to them, and become liable, that they owed something to them, until the fullest deliverer should come. It follows: "And this shall be an everlasting statute for generation and generation," never, that is, to be re [Marginal note: CHRIST] voked, just as the deliverer said, when he instituted that new sacrifice: "This cup is the new and eternal testament in my blood:" Eternal, he says, because beyond it no other shall be given, as the wise explain. It follows: "And to them, that is, to the people, you shall say: Whoever of the house of Israel, or of the sojourner in its midst, who offers a burnt offering, or a sacrifice, and does not bring it to the door of the tabernacle of testimony, to offer it to the Lord, that man shall be cut off from his people." Therefore, freed from the servitude of the devil, let us devote ourselves to God alone, offering our prayers, and sacrifices, and all our oblations to that door of testimony, who said: [Marginal note: John, same] "I am the door; if anyone enters through me, he will be saved." And he is the door of testimony, since he himself is (as John says) the faithful witness: For to this door we offer prayers and oblations, when we speak to the Father, through Jesus Christ our Lord, as through the means by which we are introduced, and obtain whatever we ask. And because it is said that the Lord smelled those sacrifices as a sweet savor, as if offered to him, and as if he delighted in the smell of crude things, we say, for some satisfaction, that all those sacrifices were offered primarily to the honor of God, although a portion was given to various powers, as necessity required: And the Lord himself smelled, not indeed those crude smokes, but delighted in the sweetness resulting from the order by which it was distributed to each, as was fitting.

Why a pair of turtledoves, or two young pigeons, were commanded to be offered for the purification of childbirth, and of a woman giving birth. Chapter XVI.

[Decorative initial 'I'] Ndeed, regarding the purification of childbirth, why by divine precept a pair of turtledoves, or two young pigeons, were offered, it is beautiful to investigate: For this (as I have learned from the wiser ones) is the reason, because even if marriage was instituted by God, nevertheless, with the greatest difficulty, due to the fall of human nature, it is exercised without fault: Which happens when spouses cohabit, so that they may generate offspring to the honor of God, and the increase of the human race: But this happens very rarely, with each one yielding to concupiscence, and lust, and the fulfillment of desire, and consequently to the infecting devil through these means, through which uncleanness is contracted. Therefore, for expelling this, and for purifying oneself—

--- Page 622 ---
**VOLUME THREE. 241**

the offspring conceived from two parents, namely, father and mother, both infected, a pair of turtledoves is offered—which are most faithful spouses and rejoice in great harmony—or two young pigeons, birds themselves most simple and replete with all harmony, and harming no one, especially the young, which are commanded to be offered. And they are endowed with such purity that the Savior, the wisdom of God, indicated the cleanness and simplicity which He requires from us through the simplicity of these animals, as if He had nothing simpler, saying: "Be simple as doves." And in the Song of Songs, the purest bride is compared to a dove by the bridegroom, who says: "My love, my dove, my beautiful one." Which also flies with such simplicity and straightness that the prophet desires to be carried on its wings to God, saying: "Who will give me wings like a dove: and I will fly away, and be at rest?" And what is greater, the Holy Spirit willed to be likened to no animal, except only to the dove, as we read in Matthew: "And behold, the heavens were opened, and he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove, and coming upon Him." And the Baptist, in John the Evangelist, says: "I saw the Spirit descending, and it remained upon Him." For it descended as a dove, which with fixed and great impetus flies downwards; or in the form of a dove, as some say, supported by the words of Luke, who says: "The heaven was opened, and the Holy Spirit descended in bodily form, like a dove, upon Him." But it is not yet concluded that it was in the form of a dove, since a dove descending upon a man does not enter into him. It seems therefore that that comparison is rather to the flight, or property, than to the form. Or if it is insisted that it also depicted a dove in figure, we will say that that figure, although corporeal, was nevertheless not dense, but subtle: so that nothing would hinder its entry into man, just as a breath, or fire, descended and entered into the Apostles. Therefore, He who purifies all was compared to the simplest and purest dove, as it is said in the Acts of the Apostles: "God sent them the Holy Spirit, that He might purify their hearts by faith." This animal, therefore, being suitable with the purifying Holy Spirit, is appropriately offered for the purification of childbirth, symbolizing the purification to be performed by the power of the Holy Spirit Himself, who is called the purifier of all sins. And because the turtledove and the pigeon agree in the same purity, therefore either of them is commanded to be offered indifferently by the poor, who do not have the means to offer a lamb—which, filled with the same purity as those birds, was offered by the richer, as the law commanded. Nor is it without mystery that turtledoves, already joined in most faithful marriage, are commanded to be offered, but the simpler young pigeons, because these indicate the offspring, while those indicate the parents to be purified. And because for the purification of one, the other is also purified, therefore one pair of these animals is commanded to be offered indifferently. But why this purification is indicated at the end of forty days is not without mystery: For just as in forty days the seed, having become an embryo, is nourished and transformed until it is brought into a perfect organic body with its due and harmonious measures, so that it may be disposed to receive a masculine soul, which is the chief faculty of man's reason, so for forty days

Why two birds were offered for cleansing a leper. Chapter XVII.
[Decorative initial C] SINCE original sin and its concupiscence were commanded to be purified by pure animals (because the most innocent child was purified along with its mother, not from malice, but from that greater concupiscence which intervened in the generation of offspring), leprosy, which indicates sin contracted by various and multiple dispositions, was commanded to be expiated by other, or common, birds: although in our translation those birds which were commanded to be offered for purifying lepers are expressed as sparrows: For צפורים Zipurim signifies birds indiscriminately, as we can understand from many places of sacred scripture, and particularly from the present text, where it is said: "Command the priest to take two live, clean zipurim," for which our translation has "from those which can be eaten:" For if Zipurim specifically meant sparrows, it would not have been necessary to add "clean," or "from those which can be eaten." [Marginal note: Origen.] Therefore, birds in general are commanded to be taken, which Origen thought were hens. But since scripture does not more clearly express what they are, admitting that they were birds in general, let us come to explain other mysteries. Two birds were commanded to be offered, one of which was sacrificed, or throttled, in an earthen vessel over living waters: The other, however, alive, with cedar wood, and scarlet, and hyssop, was dipped in the blood of the sacrificed sparrow, with which the one who was to be cleansed from leprosy was to be sprinkled seven times: and the live bird was released over the open field. Indeed, the two birds in the case of the leper indicate two conditions of the flesh: For a certain part of the flesh lives, but another part is so dead that if someone pricks it, the leper does not feel it. Therefore, the bird that is released alive indicates purification, or a sign of living flesh, and not fully infected. The other, however, was killed for the purification and re-vivification of that pre-dead flesh. This also happened...

over waters, the first and chief cleansing of all impurities, and living [waters], because dead waters are commonly putrid, defiling rather than cleansing. The living bird, however, which was released into the field, signifies that stronger flesh, or spirits not yet infected, or a better soul. But ascending to the allegorical sense, the two birds indicate two pledges which that supreme purifier Christ Jesus offered for our expiation, namely, the spiritual and the animal man: And He was slain to purge our concupiscence. [Marginal note: CHRIST.] But since it cannot be killed, it was released alive into that supreme field or plain, from which all things draw their origin: which is the Eternal Father, to whom, dying and releasing His spirit, He said: "Father, into Your hands I commend My spirit." [Marginal note: Paul] Therefore the angels said: "Why is Your garment red and stained?" Why a calf or an ox was offered along with a goat for sin. Chapter XVIII.

[Large decorative initial P] For sin, however, a goat is commanded to be offered, namely the father of the kids, who will be placed on the left to be judged, so that through the offered goat, the goat-like or kid-like part which is in man may be expiated: For there is a lustful portion in man similar to a goat, or a kid, or its mother goat, which is lustful and spoils vineyards: Therefore, it must be expiated, suppressed, bound, and led into the servitude of a better portion, just as it is said of another animal [Marginal note: Cantic.] similar to this in the Canticles: "Catch us the little foxes that spoil the vineyards." Of kids also it is said in the same place: "Feed your kids beside the shepherds' tents," namely, those who in scripture are said to feed [Marginal note: CHRI STVS] sheep well: of whom the chief is he who says: "I am the good shepherd, and I lay down my life for my sheep." Therefore, such appetites, [Marginal note: Isaias] which spoil the vineyard, must be offered and chastised—that vineyard, indeed, which (as Isaiah says) is the house of Israel, [Marginal note: CHRI STV S.] and the assembly of the elect, and the inheritance of the Lord: concerning which Christ, speaking in parables, says: "Go you also into my vineyard," into which flesh and blood, and that lustful portion, cannot enter: Therefore, it was to be offered and expiated in the goat: in which there is greater and more inveterate lust than in a kid: so much so that it stinks, just like the flesh of those who are excessively lustful, and much more than the flesh of those who live chastely. Nor is the beard, which this animal offered for sin has, devoid of mystery: For the beard signifies strength, which is manifold, and sometimes good and to be preserved, and sometimes evil and to be entirely cut off. For there is [Marginal note: Orige.] the strength and virtue of the Greeks (says Origen) in wisdom acquired by human intellects: And there is the strength of the Assyrians and Chaldeans in the knowledge of the stars and in the influence to be suspected therefrom: There is also the strength and virtue of the Persians, and Æ

--- Page 626 ---
TONVS TERTIVS.
243

...the beard signifies, not indeed that of the Nazarenes, which ought never to be shaved off, nor diminished, nor destroyed, but that which signifies the strength of those who are outside the bosom of the good, and beyond the river dividing between those gathered in Abraham's bosom, and those who are buried or are to be buried in hell, as we shall be taught by the oracle of Isaiah: [Marginal note: Isaiah.] Who, when he prophesies concerning the birth of Alma and Immanuel, who will eat butter and honey, that he may thereby learn to discern between evil and good, he adds: "In that day the Lord will shave with a hired razor those who are beyond the river, in the king of the Assyrians, the head, the hair of the feet, and the entire beard." Therefore, strength and virtue, which is according to the flesh and blood, must be shaved off or offered in sacrifice: so that this being weakened or slain, the other, namely the better part, may become stronger: Which is also more clearly explained in Deuteronomy, [Marginal note: Deut.] when it is said: "If anyone wishes to take a foreign woman as wife, her hair shall be shaved, her nails shall be cut, and she shall put off the garment in which she was captured," so that, namely, all things pertaining to the strength and virtue of paganism and carnality may be denoted as needing to be laid aside by those who are to be assumed into the bosom of the elect. This goat's beard, therefore, must either be shaved and taken away from us, or offered in sacrifice with that in which the virtue itself resides.

Also, a calf, or the king of the herd (a bull), must be offered for sin, namely, the pride and arrogance of the animal man, who glories in wickedness and rejoices when he has done evil: Which two, namely wantonness and pride, proceed from two principal sources gushing forth in the lower man, namely the concupiscible and irascible parts, which by man going to God must be offered to God himself, as Origen discusses at length and eloquently on Numbers: [Marginal note: Origen.] "The Lord," he says, "led his people by the hand of Moses and Aaron, for this reason, because the hand of one alone was not sufficient: For Moses indicates the knowledge of the law, and Aaron indeed the skill of sacrificing to God and immolating: For if, going out of Egypt and converted to God, I cast off pride: I sacrifice a bull to God himself by the hand of Aaron: but a calf, if pride and haughtiness are still tender: But if I have destroyed petulance and wantonness, I will believe that I have also slain a goat to the Lord by the hand of Aaron: Which hand of Aaron in no way offers rightly, unless regulated by the law, therefore the hand of Moses is also required. Nor would the judgment of the law suffice, unless the work is perfected by the true priest, who, according to the Apostle's saying, [Marginal note: Paul] offers himself a living sacrifice, holy, pleasing to God, with reasonable service, namely, the discretion of the law. Behold, therefore, how both hands of Moses and Aaron are required, so that the chosen people may be led into the promised land and pass through the desert of this barren age: Which Christ most perfectly accomplished, according to him who had preceded as a type: For he, observing the law even to the least, the smallest jot and tittle, offered himself, the High Priest, a living sacrifice, for a calf, for a goat, and for any burnt offering: since he himself is the whole and contains all things, as we will declare more fully in its proper place. And among other things he offered the beard, namely, the strength of the lower man, utterly mortifying it in himself, who is the head of all, as in

CHRIST. should mortify the same in all members, according to that which he said: Unless a grain of wheat falling into the earth dies, it remains alone: but if it dies, it brings forth much fruit. And this is the mystery of Christ's death, prefigured by the death of all animals which, by the command of the law, were offered in sacrifices, so that from that death he might bestow life and all the fruits of life upon us.

What the sheep, and the lamb. Chapter XIX.

ET if by law it is commanded to offer a goat, a calf, a sheep, a lamb, a cow, sparrows, turtledoves, and suchlike, yet there is one reason for offering and another: For the purification of childbirth, a lamb, or turtledoves, or two young pigeons: For the purification of lepers, sparrows: But for sin, a calf and a goat: A red heifer indeed for the universal and immense crime of the first parents and of the adored calf: But I nowhere find sheep and lambs to be offered, except for the purification of childbirth and for bringing about peace between man and God. The reason for this mystery, however, is so sublime and elevated beyond our understanding, that we scarcely dare to speak of it. But I thought it opportune to premise this, that צאן zon signifies the whole ovine family, namely, sheep, rams, male lambs, and female lambs: כשבים chebes, or כשבים chesseb, which is the same, a very tender male lamb, or female lamb, and sometimes (always, however, with a mystery) in scripture zon is placed, and sometimes one of these two: Deferring the sacrament of this matter for now, let us premise something else, that lambs or sheep, although they will be placed on the right hand of the judge to receive blessing and life, yet their origin is from a higher place, so that not without mystery our Redeemer, who proceeded from the Father, was sometimes called a lamb, sometimes a sheep.
Of him, than whom no greater arose, he says (speaking of Christ):
Ioã. Bap. "Behold the Lamb of God, behold him who takes away the sins of the world."
Isaias. But of both, Isaiah says: "As a sheep he shall be led to slaughter, and as a lamb before its shearer." And because he took care to make us all sheep, he himself, from a sheep and a lamb, became the good shepherd, so much so that he would lay down his life for his sheep. Therefore, well is the sheep, a true type of him who made peace for all things through the blood of his cross, offered for the pacification of man with God: For no one could equally well pacify us with the highest Father, as he who is in the bosom of the Father, and proceeds from him, more expressly depicted by the sheep and the lamb, both because they harm no one, but are always beneficial with manifold benefit: and also from their intrinsic property and origin, of which it is not permitted to speak at present. Hence, not undeservedly is the sheep held in such high esteem, that very great men and most pleasing to God were shepherds of sheep, such as Abel, first in the name of justice, also adorned by the testimony of the Son of God, Abraham, Father of faith and of many nations, Jacob, Father of the chosen family, and prince, and heir of God, Moses, lawgiver, and intimate with God above all prophets, David, chosen according to the heart of the Lord, first King of the tribe of Judah, singer of the Holy Spirit, and restorer and patron of the most sacred worship:
CHRIST. And finally, he himself, the Redeemer of all and Son of the Most High God: who also declares that he came only to seek the lost sheep of Israel, and

chosen family: For whose deliverance from Egypt, that is, from sin that constricts and darkens, a sheep and a lamb was offered, as it were, just as that typical one was sacrificed by the command of the law. [Marginal note: CHRIST] Indeed, to explain this mystery in detail, although it may be very difficult, nevertheless, we will touch upon something by sketching it out. It is commanded in the law that each family should take a lamb to be sacrificed and entirely eaten, so much so that if one family, being small, is not sufficient for eating it, it should take a neighbor as a guest at the feast. For every family ought to take a lamb, lest any remain deprived of the favor of the true Lamb, of whom that one bore the type. It is also commanded to be eaten whole, lest anything remain to be wasted, according to that saying of the true Lamb himself: "Gather up the fragments, lest they perish," because nothing precious ought to perish through our negligence. For bread and lamb are valued at an equal price by those who know; therefore the Redeemer wished to be called specifically bread and lamb. It ought to be male, in which a nobler and stronger virtue might flourish; and a yearling, that is, perfect in the entire course of the sun, which also signifies the Redeemer making fruitful the twelve princes, whom he established over the twelve tribes of the elect, just as He in the year makes fruitful the twelve celestial signs. It also ought to be without blemish, so that it might signify divine things, which are all whole, according to that saying of the prophet: "The works of the great God are perfect." And our [Marginal note: Mofes] Lamb says: "I have made the whole man well."

It is added that a kid also be taken with the same rite, which (as we recently said) was offered for the expiation of the animal man, just as the lamb and sheep for covenanting the better man with God, so that the whole man might make a perfect transition to the true land of promise. [Marginal note: CHRIST] But while the lamb is commanded to be sacrificed on the tenth day, the kid was kept until the fourteenth, not without mystery: For when the course of life designated by the complete number ten is finished, the perfect expiation of the animal and four-elemental man is still prolonged; because with the spirit made blessed and restored to God, who gave it for a certain course of time determined by the Father, the relief of the animal man and the four-part body from corruption, and its transition into a celestial and blessed nature, is extended. Therefore, so that it may be indicated that the whole man is to pass from Egypt to the true promised homeland of the heavens, the whole man is expiated, but first the better part through the lamb, afterwards the remaining four-part through the kid, which is therefore reserved to be sacrificed after the fourth day. But the lamb is commanded to be sacrificed and eaten with greater observance and more solemn ceremonies, because more diligent care must be taken concerning the sanctification of the celestial man, to whose sanctification also follows the sanctification of the earthly (man). And so that a clear entrance may be granted to both men, it is commanded that both doorposts be stained with the blood of the sacrificed lamb, through which both men ought to enter: indeed the better man through the right, but the other through the left, just as the sheep, pacifying him, is said to be placed on the right, and the kid, expiating this one, will be placed on the left. Indeed, these are very profound mysteries, neither a word, nor the smallest jot, is empty of mystery. Moreover, both doorposts are smeared with blood, because (as the Apostle says) [Marginal note: Paul] "Almost all things are cleansed with blood, and without the shedding of blood there is no remission." Furthermore, it is provided that nothing raw should be eaten.

Concerning the showbread, unleavened cake, wafers, similar breads, and such things anointed with oil. Chapter XX.

But since enough has been said concerning the offering of the flesh of various animals, it remains that we also briefly discuss something about breads: Which are commanded to be offered in various forms and ways, not without a profound mystery perceived by very few: Concerning which, even if it is discussed in many places, for now, however, we will explain only those things which concern the 'breads of faces' (for which we have 'showbread'), and those things which are touched upon in the seventh chapter of the book of Leviticus, which the Hebrews call 'Vayikra' in the treatise whose title among them is 'Tzav', that is, 'command': Where both a varied form of bread is described, and a manifold way of presenting it with the greatest mystery: To which all mysteries concerning breads, which are discussed elsewhere, can be reduced: For first it is commanded to take מצות חלות halot mazot, which our people have translated as 'unleavened breads'. But it was a cake, or an unleavened roll, and this kneaded with oil. Afterwards, רקיקי rechiche are required, which signify wafers: And these are commanded only to be anointed with oil. Afterwards, it is commanded to offer סולת מרבכת חלות solet murbebet halot, that is, fine flour added with a cake, and all that together kneaded and enveloped in oil: Which our translation has so intricately and confusedly, that neither the fact, nor the mystery, nor the sacrament, which is great, can be perceived: For these things, together with those which are said concerning the showbread, are most recondite secrets, and have a symbol with that unique sacrifice which our High Priest, Christ Jesus, commanded to be offered for our food and life, and in commemoration of Himself: But it is a sacrament, because through that unique bread, compacted from various grains and transformed into His body, it signifies that all of us, who are His members, must first be made into one body through charity and love, afterwards to be offered to God as a holy sacrifice, and pleasing to God Himself, so that from thence we may finally be transformed into Christ.

This power and authority He conferred upon us, just as He gave Himself to be eaten: so that, having been transformed into Him, we too, though ungrateful, may become bread of heavenly divinity, kneaded with oil and leavened by His grace and power.

**SECOND CANTICLE**
**WHAT IS TRUTH, Chapter One.**

[Marginal note: The Wise]

SO great is the splendor of truth that it overwhelms all weak eyes, and, exceeding their small power, offends them. Hence the minds of common people, and those not yet well purified, are more delighted by crude falsehood than by subtle truth; because truth is rectitude perceptible only by the mind, as the Wise define by common consent. And if it is perceived only by the mind, therefore it is not apprehended by those who in no way possess it in their mind, who neither understand those things which are of God, who is the fount of all truth: Whose proper force is the harmony and congruence of the middle with the beginning and the end.

Hence, by no small mystery, in the most ancient language (which is called holy), truth is thus described: אמת (emet). In which word the first, middle, and last letters of the alphabet, connected, come together: For א Aleph is the first, ת Tau the last, and מ Mem indeed the middle; and with their vocalizations it is pronounced 'emet'. By these letters is indicated the whole texture of things, namely, the going forth from the beginning into the thing itself, and the return to the end: And this is properly truth, and the rectitude which pertains to truth.

Moreover, to denote the firmness and stability of truth, its name is composed of letters doubly squared, namely, by figure and by numbers: For the figure of these letters is such that it has firm feet and bases, by which each of them stands separately, and all together more strongly; just as, on the contrary, the name signifying falsehood is written with letters that have no stability, nor can they stand separately, nor joined together, so that the adage is true: 'falsehood has short feet,' indeed, lame and weak. For thus that name is written שקר (sheqer), which, pronouncing in our language, we say 'secher'.

Also in numbers, all the letters from which the name of truth is composed convey a solid and firm quaternary number: For א Aleph signifies one and a thousand: Which one is the solid principle and essence of all numbers: A thousand also is the cube of the complete number ten. מ Mem, however, signifies 40, which is a number derived through the complete number ten, and through the radical quaternary number, and the solid foundation of all numbers. ת Tau, indeed, signifies 400, a number derived through ten and forty, or through four and a hundred, which is the square of ten: For ten times forty, or four times a hundred, makes 400. And thus the numbers and figures of the letters contained in the name of truth are always solid: In the letters, however, by which the name of falsehood is composed, neither the figures (as we said) nor the numbers conveyed by them contain anything of solidity; whence it is implied that falsehood easily collapses of its own accord. Moreover, it must be noted that the numbers of the letters of falsehood differ greatly from the numbers denoted by the letters of truth: For in these, one letter signifies (as we sa

--- Page 636 ---
FOURTH TONE. 248

(we said) unity and a thousand, another four tens, but the third four hundreds, indicating that truth itself apprehends and gathers divine things denoted by א aleph, celestial things by מ mem and the number forty, and terrestrial things by ת tau and the number four hundred: as is clear to those who know true formal mathematics. However, the letters from which the name of falsehood is composed, all signify hundreds, numbers indeed assigned to lower and coarser things, where falsehood and deceit thrive: For of those letters, ק coph gives one hundred, ר resh two hundred, and ש sin three hundred.

Christ is Truth. Chapter II.

[Decorative woodcut initial E]rom what has been said, it is easily understood how Christ is truth, who not only makes the middle agree with the beginning and the end, but is himself the middle, the beginning, and the end, just as He himself testifies, speaking to John in the Patmos vision, saying: I am α & ω, alpha [Marginal note: CHRIST.] & omega, the beginning and the end: For He spoke in the Greek language, just as the revelation itself was entirely written in the Greek idiom, and it is as if He had said in the Hebrew language: I am א aleph & ת tau: For of these, one is the first, and the other the last letter, just as in the Greek alphabet alpha is the first, and omega the last. Therefore, no doubt remains that Christ is the first and the last, the beginning and the end: Who again said: I am the beginning: And again: I will draw all things to myself, as it were, to the end. [Marginal note: The same] Indeed, I testified to this alone, so that the middle might also be established. Hence (as we will explain in its proper place) He was manifoldly made into the middle and a mediator. Behold then the most elegant reason why, namely, the Word of God assumed humanity, and a body, and the whole man, every kind of creature: so that, existing as the beginning, and assuming the middle, that is, man, who is intermediate between God and other creatures, containing all of them, He might lead him, and all things that are in him, to their proper end: And in this way, making the extremes and the middle agree with both, He would rightly claim the name of truth for Himself, and say: I am the truth. Moreover, He receives the name of truth, because in Him are the eternal rules, to which all must conform in life and morals: [Marginal note: The same] Hence He Himself is the moderator of all things, made the way, the door, the vine, the trunk, the rule, the teacher, the master, the regulator, directing all, and filling them with truth, because He Himself is most full, according to that of John: We saw Him full of grace and truth, from whose fullness [Marginal note: John.] we have all received.

Likewise also in the entire history [Marginal note: Paul] of Abraham, who (as Paul, discussing with the Galatians, interprets) begot two sons, signifying two testaments: one indeed in the servitude of the law, and the other in the liberty of the spirit. And just as then the son of the handmaid persecuted the son of the free woman, so also for many times since, those descending from the son of the handmaid, who are called Ishmaelites, have persecuted and persecute the co-heirs of Christ, until the time is given when there will be one fold and one shepherd: And then all things will be seen completed in clear light: Which time (unless I am mistaken) is very near: But the effects, which are narrated in the law as exhibited in the power of Christ, are almost infinite, yet all proceeding from one root: Which root is redemption, or liberation, clemency, piety, mercy, forgiveness of sin, according to that of the Apostle [Marginal note: The same]: "When you were dead in your transgressions, he made you alive together with him, having forgiven us all our transgressions, by canceling the record of debt that stood against us with its legal demands, which was contrary to us." From this mountain, therefore, full of glory and grace, the Lord appeared again, and with him thousands of saints, who (as Mat [Marginal note: Matth.] thew says) entered with him into the holy city, and appeared to many. And finally, all things are so referred to Christ, that there is no iota or tittle that is not fulfilled in him, as is clear to one who truly understands. But to write out all things individually would indeed be an inexplicable labor: Lest, however, we seem to assert these things without foundation, we will review some things in which even the smallest iota or tittle had a place in Christ, so that from a few outlined examples, the rest may be more easily believed and somewhat grasped.

How one iota, or one apex of the law, will not pass away unfulfilled and unverified in Christ. Chapter IV.

[Decorative initial I]ota is the smallest letter of the alphabet, while an apex is a point, or an accent mark. All these things are placed in scripture with due number, weight, and mystery, so much so, that Rabbi Symeon Ben Iochai and after him [Marginal note: Symeon: Elchana] Elchana, and others, not only tried to interpret sentences and words, but also to give a reason for the letters, and their figures, with apices placed below and above. And so that we may bring something forward as an example, interpreting the first word of the law, which is בראשית Beresit, they first ask why the law, and the description of the creation, begins with ב Bet.

They answer: Because ב Bet signifies a house, and indicates superior wisdom: in which all things were placed before they were brought forth into their proper forms, and through it all things were produced according to that of the Psalmographer: "You have made all things in wisdom." To which John assents, who said [Marginal note cut off]

But if the first letters of the following three words are taken, we have the same name without the last letter, which is יה: and this by a great mystery: For through that יה, they prove in that book, which is called Sepher Temunot, the Word and the divinity to be united with flesh, from which union Iesu is constituted: into whom the power of the great name of God is diffused, so that it almost seems to yield to Iesu: by which name alone it is now given for men to be saved: and it is given to us to work those miracles which used to be done by the power of that great four-letter name, as we have said elsewhere. Hence, in a wondrous order, follow another three words, whose first letters, placed in due order, form the name יֵשׁוּ Iesu. Because, therefore, this new name has been raised up, which the mouth of the Lord has named, therefore this prophetic hymn begins: "Sing to the Lord a new song." Hence the heavens, the sea, the lands, the fields, and all things that are in them, are invited to bring forth the praises of this Christ of ours, to whom the Father gave a name which is above every name. Indeed, it would be long to unravel all passages of sacred scripture with their mysteries, since none is devoid of its sacrament: Therefore, having brought these few as examples, we will come to the points, which are twofold: For the lower ones, which for the most part are called points, but in Hebrew נְקֻדּוֹת necudot, signify the vivifying spirit, both hovering and brooding over all members, whether of the mundane or the mystical body, about which the scripture speaks. Seeing this, Ezekiel said: "And the spirit of life was in the wheels," namely, the mundane and the human, vivifying both. But the upper points, which are called accents by us, but in Hebrew טְעָמִים, signify the divine and holy spirit, sanctifying and returning to God: Concerning this twofold spirit, which nevertheless is one, Origen speaks in *Peri Archon* [Origen] not in-II in.

Christ perfected the law. Chapter V.

[Illuminated initial N depicting a figure, possibly Christ or a saint, within the letter]
NOR did he merely confirm the law by fulfilling all things contained in it, as he himself testified, saying: "I have not come to abolish
[Marginal note: CHRISTUS.]
the law, but to fulfill it," but he also perfected it, and led it to a better degree through the Gospel, which signifies good news, just as if someone were to take lead type characters of printers arranged on a tablet to express some harsh things, and then re-adapted them to express sweeter and more sublime words, while the shape of the characters remained the same: In a similar way, Christ acted, not inventing another law, but perfecting the same law, and leading it to a better destiny, so that it might seem different, though it is not, but the same, just as a cloth, when dyed with scarlet or some precious color, is perfected and not changed. Therefore, the law was perfected, dyed and colored with the blood of Christ much more happily than when sprinkled with the blood of animals,
[Marginal note: Paulus]
as the Apostle says: "Christ, having come as a high priest of the good things to come, through the greater and more perfect tabernacle, which was indeed Christ himself, true and living, not made with hands, that is, not of this creation: nor through the blood of goats or calves, but through his own blood, he entered once for all into the holy places:" From these words we clearly have that Christ, in his own blood, expanded and perfected the law: He expanded it indeed, because that law, which was observed by the single Israelite family and a few foreigners in the small region of Judea and Phoenicia, was diffused by Christ throughout the entire world and among all
