**TONVS SEXTVS. 290**

It is given: For JESUS is the beginning signified by א, just as He Himself testifies, saying: I am the beginning, who speak to you. And in Him is the nature of the Trinity, while [Marginal note: CHRIST.] He says of the Father: The Father is in me: And again: I and the Father are one. Of the Holy Spirit also He says: He will receive from what is mine. From these things we gather the nature of the Trinity, and that the beginning is in Him, from which it is fitting for Him to have the name importing those two things. And from this we can infer how also the power of the supreme name is contained in Jesus: for that is אהיה (Ehyeh) beginning with א and containing י and a double ה. By which א, to those knowing the mysteries of letters, is denoted the first beginning and the ultimate end, since it signifies one and a thousand, which is the cube of ten, and of the last simple number: Similarly, י signifies the beginning, as its interpretation indicates, and signifies the end, since it is a letter signifying the ultimate number: Hence both letters are divine, and both signify the beginning and the end, which is the same thing: because that which is the beginning of things is also their end: One ה is figured by another: For א is figured from two י's with one ו interposed transversally: Therefore, in the four-letter name, and in the name Jesus, י is placed for א, and for ו itself: And thus we have in the name Jesus the mystery of two letters, and their significations in the one named Himself: because Jesus Himself is the beginning (as we recently said) and is the end giving rest and blessedness. There are also in that supreme name two ה's signifying two emanations of the producer into the things produced: In all these productions the Son intercedes, except for His own production from the Father: Hence He said: My Father works until now, [Marginal note: The same.] and I work, namely, producing all things with Him. Nor let us proceed further in declaring mysteries of this kind, although there are very many. Since therefore the power and mysteries of all names are contained in the name of Jesus, it is no wonder if Paul says that in this name every knee bows, of those in heaven, on earth, [Marginal note: Paul.] and under the earth.

Why only the name of Jesus is invoked today by true worshippers of God. Chapter VIII.

[Decorative initial C containing a figure] Since we have declared all names, and their virtues of every kind, to be contained in Jesus and His name, deservedly we invoke that name alone, according to the prophecy of Zechariah, in which he says: And the Lord will be king [Marginal note: Zacha.] over all the earth, and in that day the Lord will be one, and His name one. Nor is anyone found who has been king of the whole earth and Lord, except Jesus, under whom, with idolatry destroyed, all had Him as King and Lord, with the exception of a few scattered Hebrews, until that beast Mahumeth arose: Nor yet from that time was another name given to men by which they could be saved, except the name of JESUS, as Peter said in the Acts of the Apostles: Which he ordered to be spread among [Marginal note: Peter.] all nations, just as the four-letter name was known only among the Israelite people: For he said to Ananias concerning Paul: This man is a chosen vessel to me, [Marginal note: CHRIST.] that he may bear my name before Gentiles, and kings, and the children of Israel: which he also did: For immediately from Damascus he went to Jerusalem, then to Tarsus, the metropolis of Cilicia, then to Antioch, an excellent city of Syria, afterwards to Phrygia, Galatia, Troy,

...Macedonia, and Athens, where the wisdom of the world flourished. After these, to Corinth, Ephesus, Miletus, Cos, Rhodes, and through those islands of Achaia and Greece, traveling further, he proceeded to the Arabs, and came into Italy: and he traveled as far as the Spaniards through Asia and Europe, carrying and spreading the name of Jesus: And what remained of the world, the other Apostles completed by the power of this name [Marginal note: CHRIST], so that all and everything could be sought in the name of Jesus, just as He Himself taught, saying: 'Whatever you ask the Father in my name, He will give you:' Of whose name [Marginal note: Paul] there is such power, that all can be enriched in it, as Paul says: 'Rich unto all who invoke Him,' that is, the name JESUS, which is so gentle, so communicable, and diffusive of itself, that it is compared to oil in the Canticles, where it is said: 'Your name is oil poured out,' because its virtue, full of chrism, is diffused into those whom it touches, like oil on cloth: and because it heals, because it preserves, and does all things, like true oil to those who know how to receive and invoke it, just as the Apostles did: For in His name they spoke in tongues, cast out demons, healed the sick: For Peter [Marginal note: Peter] said to the lame man sitting at the Beautiful Gate of the temple: 'Silver and gold I have none, but a better treasure, namely the power of the name of Jesus, in which I command you to rise and walk:' and immediately his feet and ankles were strengthened: and leaping up, he stood walking, and entering the temple, praising God.

Indeed, the power of that name flows, when it is duly invoked, like a river from a spring: For (as Democritus [Marginal note: Democ Epicu.] says, and after him Epicurus) a voice and a sounding name is like a current, or a channel conveying the word of the mind, which is like a spring, giving power to the uttered word and conceiving it: But the true channels of divine names are in the Hebrew idiom with their characters, by which those names were first described with the greatest mystery: Hence Iamblichus [Marginal note: Iambli.] says: 'The Gods, that is, angels acting with us, approved the barbaric language, namely Hebrew, as sufficiently congruent, especially because it was the older and first mode of speaking:' But let us add this: because those characters, both from imported numbers and from the figuration of celestial things, are wonderful and mysterious: Therefore [Marginal note: Zoroa.] Zoroaster, most skilled in working, teaches that barbaric words, that is, Hebrew words, should not be changed in sacred rites: Which the Catholic Church has also observed in many places, as when it commanded to say 'alleluia,' which means 'praise Yah' (יה), which is a divine name of utmost importance, and fruitful of the tetragrammaton name, because with those two full letters it yields in number 26, which is the number of the four-letter name: So also that 'Adonai Lord:' and that 'osianu,' for which we say 'hosanna:' and that, 'Lord God zebaot,' for which the corrupted word 'sabbaot' is said: for this word ('sabbaot') sounds 'rest' in the plural: but that ('zebaot') means 'armies:' for here it should be said 'Lord God of armies.' And the name of our redeemer should be written with only three letters, full of its mystery, namely YHV (יהו). Nor should the letter He (ה) be added as a combination, as some have thought, because those (letters) are already (as we have said) converted into Shin (ש). Nor should a second Shin (ש) be appended by saying YHShW (יהושו), although it is said in Latin, following the order of grammatical declension: About which we do not care much...

...it is not very important, because mysteries are not in the Latin idiom, but in Hebrew, where care must be taken not to add or subtract anything: because many mysteries would be destroyed, which are contained as much in the meanings of the letters of that name, as in their numbers, and also in corresponding prophecies: from which we will briefly touch upon some or a few. The more recondite Theologians [Marginal note: Theolo.] hold it as constant that oracles often contain the names of those about whom prophecy is made, at the beginning, end, or middle of words: according to which method the name of the Messiah is frequently found, as in the verse of the seventy-first psalm: 'Before the sun His name endures, and in Him shall all the tribes [Marginal note: psalm.] of the earth be blessed.' For the name ישו Iesu (Jesus) is contained in the initial letters of these words, 'permanet nomen eius, & benedicentur' (His name endures, and they shall be blessed), which in Hebrew are thus said: ינון שמו וית ברכו (inin semo ueit barcu): where if the initial letters of the words are taken, which are י ש ו, they constitute ישו Iesu (Jesus): Which name was before the sun, and in Him all nations were blessed. Similarly in the book [Marginal note: Gen: 49.] of Genesis, chapter 49, where it is said: 'Let the Messiah come, and to Him shall they be gathered,' the initial letters of the words constitute the name Iesu, which in Hebrew are thus said: יבא שלו ולו (iabo silo uelo). For the initial letters are י ש ו: Which letters, placed in Hebrew order, render ישו (Iesu). But more wonderfully, in the ninety-fifth psalm, in those words: 'Let the heavens rejoice, and let the earth exult, let the sea tremble, and all its fullness; let the fields exult, and all that is in them': In the initial letters of these words is found the complete four-letter name: And afterwards the same name without the last ה: Then the name Iesu, to denote that that four-letter name ought to be encompassed in the name Iesu, as its successor, to whom it in a certain way yielded, because the power of that four-letter name was given to Iesu, to whom the Father gave all things: Whence the author of Sepher Temunot [Marginal note: Se. Te.] proves by that last ה of the four-letter name itself, that divinity ought to be united with humanity, and become Messiah, in whom the power of that great name would exist: Therefore the names are united, and the name Iesu succeeds that incomplete four-letter name, when it is repeated a second time: Because, just as in the prior testimony the complete name was venerated, so in the second and last it is implied to have yielded (as we said) to our Iesu: For the Hebrew words of the text of that psalm are thus found: ישמחו השמים ותגל הארץ ירעם הים ומלואו יעלוז שדי וכל: The initial letters of which words, placed in Hebrew order, are יהו ה יהו ש.

But since we are discussing the letters of the name Iesu, I deemed it opportune to also explain why, from the interpretation of the letters, no more letters should be found in it, since these perfectly convey what is contained in the one named by this name ישו (Iesu): For י signifies the beginning, ו itself, and ש the beginning of Sabbath, hinting at rest itself, and the end. They denote, therefore, that He Himself is the beginning, the end, and the rest of all things, just as in the Apocalypse [Marginal note: Apocal.] He Himself says: 'I am α and ω: the beginning and the end.' And since all things are included in these words, those letters suffice, nor should others be added. Furthermore, this name ישו (Iesu) is completed from the greater, lesser, and middle numbers into a denary, which is a complete number: For it is a six, one ten, and three hundreds, which, joined together, constitute ten, indeed a perfect number, and constituted from all kinds of things, namely spiritual, celestial, and terrestrial, which are conveyed by numbers, denaries,

But leaving aside lesser things, so that we may speak of higher things, I say that all the supernal waters of graces and gifts are collected in him, as in a true upper pool, of which it is said in the Canticles: [Canti.] Your eyes are like pools in Heshbon, that is, in thought or word, in which all things were contained before they were created: for Heshbon signifies thoughts leading to the word: Hence, where we have, In the beginning was the word, in Hebrew it is בראשית היה חשבון (bereshit hayah heshbon), that is, there was thought, word, pool, in which all things were contained before they were created. These are few, or very small, in comparison to those things which could be said about this most holy name, which was named by God, announced by an angel, imposed by parents, celebrated by the world, venerated by every kind, and placed for salvation for all, yet for error for demons, and for power for those who work: For in seraphim it inflames with fiery power: In cherubim it shines: In thrones it binds together: In dominations it commands: In virtues it executes: In powers it restrains: In principalities it cares for provinces, princes, and magistrates: In archangels, performing priestly office, it directs mortals to God: In angels it cares for all our things: In man, by the bond of all things, it works all things: For it teaches and speaks in various tongues in the apostles: it shines with truth in evangelists and doctors: it is diffused with power in those who work miracles: it fills contemplatives with sweetness: it grants pardon to penitents: and every kind of help to all in need. Nor should we proceed further to the particular virtues of this name, in which all things must now be sought by us: because since we have demonstrated that all things are included in him and depend on him, I would deem it superfluous to labor through each one individually.

How we have Christ prefigured from sacred scripture as the fount of all merit, grace, and glory. Chapter IX.

**V**T the named one may correspond to the name, just as we have proven that all things are contained in the name, so it is necessary that in the named one himself is contained all virtue, all merit, and all grace, from whom, as from the fount of the true paradise of delights, the whole earth is watered. But leaving aside what has already been treated as trivial by our Theologians in their proper places, we will only briefly touch upon some things which are hidden in the divine oracles: And first, we will unravel those things which have been prefigured by deeds: afterwards, those which have been foretold by divine oracles: For when the Pharisees sought a true sign of the Messiah's advent, [CHRI STVS.] Christ responded: This generation seeks a sign, and no sign will be given to it except the sign of Jonah.

For he was a shadowy and figurative savior, destined only for one people, who, having relapsed, finally perished. But Christ, the true savior for the whole human race, entered once into the holy places, eternal redemption having been found, giving us continuously grace, by which we can do those things which pertain to salvation, and imparting of the merits acquired for us, and finally bestowing glory most abundantly prepared. Whence by His grace we do good, and by His merits we come to salvation and glory.

Through which blood He redeemed us, paid all debts, and acquired for us all grace and merit, as Peter says: "To obedience and sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ: Grace to you and peace be multiplied."
How clearly Isaiah revealed all these things in a single oracle. Chapter XI.
Isaias. [marginal note] [Decorative initial I] saiah, however, describes this matter so openly that it seems not a prophecy but an already manifested gospel (as Jerome says): For he says: "The Lord has prepared His arm, and indeed His right arm, that is, of mercy and and grace, in the eyes of all nations:" Which arm was previously extended only to the Israelite people: From which follows: "All the ends of the earth shall see the salvation, or the health, or the savior of our God," whom He will send, of course, for the redemption of all. Afterwards, the prophet, directing his discourse to the Gentiles, adds: "Depart, depart from the worship, namely, of demons and idols: Touch no unclean thing," that is, things offered to idols. "Go out from the midst of her," that is, from the worship of idolatry, "and be clean from all your defilements and pollutions."
"You who bear the vessels of the Lord," that is, you who have receptive capacities for divinity, so much so that you are called the temple and dwelling place of God: or you who perform the priestly office, no longer offer to your idols the vessels which you ought to give to the Lord: the vessels, indeed, in which you place sacrifices, or the vessels that are yourselves, as the oracle said of Paul: "This man is a chosen vessel to me:" Or (as Jerome understands it) you Apostles, who bear the vessels, that is, the power by which you can baptize the people, depart from the obstinate, blasphemous, and wicked Jews, for whose destruction the Roman army is prepared.
Nor shall you depart in haste, as they once did from Egypt, but the Lord, and the Prince of Peace, will go before you, who says: "I am with you always, even to the consummation of the age." This work, therefore, though arduous, will be done without clamor and tumult: because it will be without the slaughter of peoples, indeed, with their salvation, although many will suffer death as a testimony to the preached faith and doctrine:
Sapien. [marginal note] because it will be done with the peace of those who endure, as it is said in the Book of Wisdom: "In the sight of the unwise they seemed to die, and their departure was taken for misery: but they are in peace." And this is what the prophet continues with: "For we shall undertake this work not in tumult, nor shall you go out from it with tumult, nor shall you hasten to execute it with flight:" "For the Lord will go before you, and the God of Israel will gather, or associate, you."
"Behold, my servant," that is, the truly Israelite people, "shall understand, and shall be exalted, and shall be lifted up, and shall be exceeding high:" For from him were chosen the Apostles, who were appointed over the universal Church, and constituted as assessors of the prince, who himself also drew his origin from the same Israelite people, and many others from the same stock were exalted in various ways. And "as many were astonished at you," when, namely, I drew you out of Egyptian servitude, and set you over the nations, and exalted you with many wonders and miracles, and gave you dominion over nations and kingdoms, "so shall they be astonished at this Redeemer."

For all of us, like sheep, have gone astray, each one has turned to his own way, all were subject to sins and iniquities, and to those liabilities, from which they could not be rescued: Therefore the Lord laid upon him the iniquities of us all: Which work, although with the resistance of the sensitive part, yet he voluntarily undertook: whence it follows: "He was offered, because he himself willed it." Hence he said to Peter, who was trying to rescue him from the hand of those capturing him: [CHRIST] "The cup, which the Father has given me, do you not wish that I drink it?" And when Peter previously abhorred the name and work of the cross, he said to him: "Get behind me, Satan, you are a stumbling block to me, for you do not savor the things that are of God, but those that are of men." Because therefore he voluntarily undertook this work, for that reason he did not open his mouth in his own defense, but stood as if mute before Herod and Pilate, who were seeking to free him: whence it follows. "Like a sheep he will be led to slaughter, and like a lamb before its shearer he will be silent:" Indeed he was the Lamb taking away the sins of the world, and all crimes, which could not be expiated by any sacrifice, sacrificed in the true Passover, and passage to a better life.

Therefore, because of the anguish endured for us, and the judgment, and the sentence which he sustained for us, he was accepted and glorified. And since he did those things which no man can do, therefore he is proven to be above man: whence the prophet adds: "Who will declare his generation?" For he was cut off from the land, not of the dying, but of the living, who had come to give us life. "For the iniquity of my people he was struck," or "a wound was inflicted upon him," so that it may be the voice of the eternal Father, or of the prophet narrating, although we have "he was struck" so that it may be expressly understood that it is the paternal voice. It follows: "And he will grant his burial to the wicked," that is, by his death and burial he will grant the sins of the peoples, and will obtain pardon for them: "And he will acquire riches in his death:" Indeed he will be rich towards all who will invoke that name which the Father gave him: because he became obedient even unto the death of the cross. Nor did he commit iniquity, nor was deceit found in his mouth, [yet] it was necessary for him to suffer for the expiation he himself provided: therefore for our sake the Lord willed to crush him. [Large decorative initial C containing a landscape scene] Since therefore our Messiah and Christ has been, through whom all things were made before, and is the author and finisher of faith, and filling all things with his divinity, existing as part and whole, and in a certain way existing as all things in all things, vivifying all members of the mystical body, like the human soul, extending himself even to artificial things and our works, as we can learn from the proper name full of sacraments and his cognomens imposed not by chance, but from events and accommodated mysteries, so much so that only his name is invoked by true worshipers: and since he himself has taken upon himself all our weaknesses, infirmities, and debts, so that we, being free, may work more readily, he has deservedly become the one through whom we do all things, as Paul says: "I can do all things [Marginal note: Idem.] through him who strengthens me." **THAT CHRIST IS THE TRUE LORD FORETOLD BY MOSAIC PROPHECIES.**
**Chapter One.**

[Large decorative initial V] TO RELATE, even in part, what the Holy Spirit foretold through the mouths of the prophets concerning the dominion and kingdom of our Christ, we must begin with Moses. For the Lawgiver [Marginal note: Moses.] when speaking of the generation of man, seems to describe his production twice: First, he relates that He created them male and female, in His image and likeness: Afterwards, as if he had said nothing about man, he says in the following [verses]: "Nor was there a man to work the ground, whence the Lord God formed man from the dust of the earth, or from the dust of the ground, and breathed into his face the breath of life." Nor is it to be thought that so great a man, most learned in all wisdom, full of God, and imbued with the Holy Spirit, was struck with such dullness as to forget what he had said a little earlier, and repeat his formation again, whom he had already described as made in the likeness and image of God, and constituted Lord of all things: And by the same reasoning, after he had related that male and female had been produced, he immediately, forgetting what he had said, adds: "And for man there was not found a helper like himself, or one that stood before him," as the truth of the letter has it: For who could ascribe such mental sluggishness to so great a man, that he should repeat the same thing twice in vain, he who did not insert even a superfluous iota in his description? Therefore, to remove this apparent error from a man full of God and from the sacred scriptures, we reveal from the most sacred treasuries (as those most skilled in these matters affirm) that Moses first described the Messiah and the production of his mother: Of whom Christ is with the true image of God, and the firstborn of all, as Paul says: [Marginal note: Paul] "Who is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature." And He himself was made male, and she herself female, in the divine mind, first, and before, and above all others: To whom also He subjected all things, saying: "Have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the birds of the air, and over the beasts of the earth, and over all living things that move upon the earth:" Singing of this, the divine Psalmist [Marginal note: David] says: "You have crowned him with glory and honor, and have set him over the works of your hands: You have subjected all things under his feet, all sheep and oxen, moreover also the beasts of the field, the birds of the air, and the fish of the sea, and those who walk the paths of the sea." And that this is sung of Christ, Paul, the revealer of mysteries, explains with open speech to the Corinthians and [Marginal note: Paul] Hebrews, saying that those things were foretold of Christ, and coming to that word, "You have subjected all things under his feet," he says: [Marginal note: The same] "In that he subjected all things, he left nothing not subjected, except him who subjected all things, to whom that Son was subjected:" Whom (as it follows with the Hebrews) we saw, because of the suffering of his death, crowned with glory and honor (as it is said in the psalm). To whom, male and female, it was said: "Increase and multiply," not indeed by carnal multiplication, but by spiritual and divine [multiplication], as it has happened: so much so, that from the fulness

who put an end to the kingdom of Judah, with King Zedekiah led captive into Babylon, and the city and temple devastated: so much so that there was never afterwards a king in Jerusalem, nor in the house of Judah: And they say that this Nebuchadnezzar was the expectation of the nations: because under him the dominion and empire of the nations was expanded: But these are truly more to be laughed at and hissed at than listened to: because Shiloh does not signify "one sent": nor was Nebuchadnezzar the expectation of the nations, nor were other nations gathered to him, other than the Chaldeans, Persians, and Medes, which are but a small part in respect to other nations. Nor did the Jewish scepter entirely fail under Nebuchadnezzar: because after the people were brought back from captivity, there were many leaders in that tribe. Others say that it took place in Saul, who was of the tribe of Benjamin, anointed king in Shiloh: because then the glory of the kingdom and the scepter of Judah passed to the tribe of Benjamin: Which is no less ridiculous than the first: since the scepter of the kingdom had not been taken away from Judah, for the decree of God, that that tribe should have a king, had not yet been put into execution, just as it had always been royal by divine sanction. Therefore (as the wiser Hebrews say) Jacob believed more in the promise made by Judah for Benjamin's return, than in the other ten sons
[Marginal note: Genesis] vouching for him, as we read in the book of Genesis. This royal scepter, therefore, was granted by God to the tribe of Judah from the beginning, granted for a short time to the tribe of Benjamin, and immediately restored to the tribe of Judah in David, while Saul was still alive: And the kingdom endured in that family for fourteen generations, until the Babylonian captivity: after which there were still leaders from the tribe of Judah, such as Zerubbabel, and those who followed. Nor was Saul anointed in Shiloh, but in Kiriath-jearim (as some say) or in the land of Zuph, as it is found in the first book of Kings. But he now rules much more felicitously in it, although he has fixed his seat in the heavens: for a name has been given to him, to whom every knee bows, of those in heaven, on earth, and under the earth. This therefore is the Messiah, Christ, and anointed above all as true king, priest, and prophet, to whom all nations are gathered, as it is found in the text ולו יקהת עמים (velo ichebat bamim): which is thus interpreted word for word: And to him shall be gathered a nation, or a people: For which our translation has: And he will be the expectation of the nations. For indeed, to no one reigning from the Israelite family have the nations been gathered, so that they might obey his dominion, except to Christ: to whom the whole world has adhered, and from every nation under heaven: for he will draw all, even enemies, to himself by his power, as the oracle had previously said: Your hands are on the necks of your enemies, and the sons of your Father will worship you, of the heavenly Father, indeed, who rules over all, and is called the Father of all. **SEVENTH TONE. 298**

The same is confirmed by other prophecies. Chapter II.

[Decorative initial V] Seeing that other Prophets have foretold concerning this dominion and kingdom given to our Jesus, we will briefly touch upon some of the many: For David, speaking in his own person [Marginal note: Dauid] in the second psalm, says: The Lord said to me: You are my Son, this day I have begotten you: where in Hebrew it is היום ילדתיך (baiom ielidtica): by which word 'baiom' is understood eternity without any determined time, as the author of the book called, Eloquia [Marginal note: Au. &c.] pulchritudinis, rightly interprets. Therefore, it speaks of Him begotten from eternity, and born temporally according to the flesh: Ask of me, and I will give you the nations for your inheritance, and the ends of the earth for your possession: Ask, that is, by performing the work which I have established, so that you may have legitimate dominion over all the ends of the earth: Which He had, and has, although the Mahometan schism was permitted by divine dispensation, not without order and mystery: concerning which there would be a great discourse, but I will only adduce what Paul, conscious of God's secrets, writes prophetically to the Thessalonians: [Marginal note: Paulus] Let no one terrify you, or seduce you by word or by letter, as if the day of the Lord were at hand: for it will not come, that is, showing the authority of His empire on the seat of His majesty, unless the dissension comes first: which truly and greatly happened through Mahomet: and also the man of sin, the son of perdition, will have been revealed, who will oppose and exalt himself above all that is called God: whence he will be called antichrist, and antideus, that is, against Christ and God: But the Lord Jesus will kill him with the spirit of His mouth, and will restore those things which have been torn apart by the Mahometan beast. Then He will rule all things with a rod of iron, that is, with insurmountable and utterly invincible power: and like a potter's vessel He will break them, namely the beast with its sect, and the son of iniquity with his father the devil, who has the empire of death: then indeed, death, the enemy, will be destroyed. **Why Christ is not said to reign in the house of Abraham, although the promise concerning Him was first made to Abraham himself. Chapter III.**

[Large decorated initial A] braham, beyond all doubt, was called the father of the chosen family, the father of faith, existing as the head, as we are taught in the Gospel, to whose bosom all the elect flowed: nevertheless the heavenly oracle, when it announced the conception of the Redeemer, did not say, "He will reign in the house of Abraham," but "He will reign in the house of Jacob": Which I believe was because it was said to Abraham: "Cast out the handmaid and her son": In this, Abraham bears the image of a great and universal father, who has good and bad sons, just and unjust, upon whom He rains and causes His sun to rise: Therefore, not without mystery, from Abram he was called Abraham, that is, Father of many and mixed nations: Who also, in his offspring and progeny, holds the image of that father: For he had Isaac from a legitimate marriage, and Ishmael from an illegitimate one. But, alas, where am I venturing? What will be the legitimate and illegitimate marriage of the paternal and divine mind, so that Abraham there can hold its image? Indeed, there was a legitimate marriage for the Father, when from eternity that divine eye beheld His own essence as His proper wife, or (as they say) His proper object, and the seeing intellect and the seen essence became two not in one flesh, but in one most fruitful mind: which is also called the Father, generating His beloved Son, deservedly named Isaac, that is, laughter and delight, of the Father, namely. "This is (said that paternal voice) My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased": And this is the legitimate son, who, naturally begotten, endowed with all dignity and every privilege, was constituted heir of all things, through whom He also made the ages. But who Ishmael, born of an illegitimate marriage, might have been, it is impious at first glance even to consider this, that the Eternal Father had a son from a marriage other than a legitimate one: Yet the discourse does not offend prudent ears, although pious ones may fear to hear it. Let it be said, I ask, how angelic minds and all other things outside God were produced by the common parent of all: Not indeed from the legitimate and natural union of that paternal mind with the divine essence, because from that only His only-begotten Son proceeded, but undoubtedly from another, that is, by a complacent intuition He produced the ideas of all things in His mind, to the limits of which exemplars He fashioned all external things: Which knowledge of ideas, and production of things, spurious in a way—

Therefore, touched by envy and puffed up by pride, that wicked one began to persecute him, whence from a most worthy creature, he was made a most hideous dragon. And the dragon stood (says **John**), who is the devil, to devour the son of the woman clothed with the sun, and crowned with twelve stars: But the son was taken up, and it was said in heaven: "Cast out the handmaid and her son," that is, the delight had in producing that most noble creature along with the son himself who was produced: And that great dragon, who is the devil, was cast out. Some will perhaps be struck with incredible wonder, asking: "How was he born from an external delight and from God, who became the devil, and by what means also were he and the delight, which was about producing and preserving him, cast out, since in God there is neither external delight, nor is anything cast out as reprobate from the supreme good?" To whom we can sufficiently answer, declaring that if God, being most good, is happy without any external good, and needing none of our goods, indeed, bestowing all those things upon us, **Solomon** nevertheless, bearing his person, sings in Proverbs: "And my delights are with the sons of men." And if he delights in human minds, it is fitting that he also delights in higher, or angelic, [beings]. He also delights in each of the creatures he produced, as he had said a little earlier: "And I delighted day by day," that is, in every form appearing in my creatures, whatever it may be: For this is proper to any artist, to delight, namely, in the works of his hands, in which he perceives and beholds an image or likeness of himself, which nature itself brings a wonderful delight to the artist. Nor is there to me a more elegant reason why God loves creatures so much, unless because he perceives something of his own in the work, and beholds his image, or a trace. Nor is the delight proceeding from an external work, but it flows from the craftsman himself along with the idea and form of things, which all are drawn from the supernal exemplar: Which delight, when it passes into creatures, deservedly obtains the name of handmaid. Therefore, he drives her from his royal house with her son, when someone, having become impure or rebellious, is found unworthy of such a banquet and kingdom. Therefore, that wicked and rebellious one was first expelled from that kingdom with his followers—

Therefore, the peaceful king ought not to reign in that family, in which there are still enemies and rebels, until all are placed as a footstool for his feet.

Concerning which place it is said that its foot was on the earth, that is, in our heart made from earth: which ought to be a certain valley of tears, since for us, while [Marginal note: CHRIST] we inhabit the earth, there must be weeping, according to the edict of the highest Emperor, so that we may be comforted in our homeland. lives, namely the active and the contemplative: to which he applies and joins two portions, the higher and the lower: For no one is of Christ's family unless he exercises himself in the active life with Martha, or the contemplative life with Mary, or in both with the Apostles. The active life is therefore figured in Leah, who is called laborious, and has bleary eyes, and eyes hindered from clear vision, indicating that the mind occupied with external works is troubled by many things, so that it cannot perfectly devote itself and apply its inner eye to divine matters: The contemplative life, however, is in Rachel, who is interpreted as 'seeing the beginning,' and is most beautiful: because the eye of the mind, and that supreme portion devoted to contemplation, gazes upon God, the beginning of all things: who, since He is most beautiful, it is necessary that the eye contemplating Him be beautiful, as Plotinus says: "Let him become beautiful and God-like, if he is to behold divine beauty." [Marginal note: Plotinus] But let the order (I ask) of this matter be observed: Jacob sighs for Rachel and serves for her, and yet is first joined to Leah, because the spiritual man sighs for the quiet and vision that is in contemplation: for which he undertook the yoke of God's service: nevertheless, it is necessary that he first be joined to Leah and the active life, before he arrives at contemplative perfection: Therefore, those ancient fathers decreed that no one should be admitted to the solitary and contemplative life unless they had been exercised for eighteen or twenty years in works of charity and the services of the monastery: For this is the custom of the homeland and of the family devoted to God, that a person, purged through works of penance and laborious efforts, may ascend to the sweet contemplation of divine things: for which he serves for repeated seven-year periods, by which a man, doubly purified and initiated into God, may be able to call [upon Him]: For the number seven is critical, purgative, and remissive. Critical indeed, because in it changes and renewals commonly occur: For an infant, whether it will live, is discerned in the seventh hour: and after seven days it casts off the remnants of the umbilical cord: and after twice seven [days] its sight begins to move towards the light: and after seven times seven [days] it freely turns its pupils and whole face towards individual fears concerning what is to be seen: But after seven months, teeth begin to emerge from the jaws: and after twice seven [months] it sits without fear of falling: After thrice seven [months] its sound breaks forth into words: After four times seven [months] it not only stands firmly, but walks: After five times seven [months] it begins to dislike its nurse's milk: In the seventh year, teeth are changed to more suitable ones, and in the same year the perfection of speech is fully achieved: and having completed the second seven-year period, it reaches puberty and begins to be moved by the power of generation: In the third [seven-year period] it shows blossoms and down [facial hair]: In the fourth [seven-year period] the growth of stature is defined: In the fifth [seven-year period] youthful perfection is completed: In the sixth [seven-year period] the previously gathered strengths are preserved: In the seventh [seven-year period] it perfects its age, so that it is fit for counsel. But when it has reached seven decades, where the number seven is brought to its full measure by a complete number [ten], [Marginal note: David] then it has the common limit of living, as the prophet says: "The days of our years are seventy years." And through this number seven, authors of medicine determine that many alterations occur in fevers. [Marginal note: Auth. m. 7] We have briefly touched upon these things, so that it may be understood that the service of twice seven [years] is not described without reason—

--- Page 745 ---
**OF THE SECOND CANTICLE**

a path made by man, who wishes to devote himself to God and to contemplation: To which if he wishes to arrive, it is necessary that he be twice changed and transformed from clarity to clarity, so that he may fix the eye of his mind without offense to it on those eternal spectacles. And by the same number is indicated the purification to be performed, when he has been purified: Therefore Elisha, not ignorant of this mystery, commanded that Naaman be washed seven times in the Jordan. And in the law it is holy that a cleansed leper be sprinkled seven times in the blood of a sparrow. And because expiation occurs in the septenary, remission also follows the same number, as we are taught in a long series in Leviticus, that is, that in the seventh year debts would be remitted, and fields would rest, no exaction being made from them through cultivation. In the seventh square, however, there was a full remission of debts, of servants, and of all things that had been alienated. Hence Peter, when he spoke of remission, proposed the septenary number, saying: "Lord, how often shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? Up to seven times?" From which number Christ, responding, did not wish to depart, but said: "I do not say to you up to seven times, but up to seventy times seven," bringing the septenary to completion by means of the denary number. And for his prudence the steward of iniquity is praised, who not without mystery reduced one hundred to fifty: so that from this he might more easily obtain remission, as Jerome discusses to Galasius, and Theophilus with him. Finally, the Redeemer observed this number in the mission of the Holy Spirit, who came after the same square, just as in the law a full remission was given in the fiftieth year itself. Therefore, Jacob, rightly laboring with this number, purified, obtained remission, and twice changed for the better, came to his Rachel, who prefigures contemplation.

But let us return to the two wives, each of whom has her handmaid. Therefore, the legitimate wives are the active life and the contemplative life, in which two powers of Jacob delight, namely intellect and will: or (as academics teach) that superior portion of the intellect, which some call synderesis, and the rational and discursive portion, of which the latter serves the active life, and the former the contemplative. But it is a wondrous mystery, how each of them offers her handmaid. Indeed, that superior and contemplative portion has a handmaid, by whom contemplating these created and lower things, it may be delighted: through which visible things it may ascend to the invisible creator: And this is the discursive reason annexed to the senses, through which it perceives sensible things: and our Jacob is joined to it, when through these lower things observed he hunts for the magnitude of the creator: But he is joined to Rachel, when he beholds and contemplates the very principle of things, and the fount of all good things, in the light emanating from Him, with the eye of the mind. The inferior portion also has, or the will, or the operative virtue, its handmaid, namely delight in things to be done: to which delight, or co-delighting virtue, if Jacob is joined, and the spiritual man directing all things to God, she herself also bears good fruits worthy of eternal life: He is joined to Leah, when he acts immediately for God. But let us also observe the names of the handmaids, if they are fitting: Rachel's handmaid is Bilhah, who is said to be "absorbed" or "grown old"—

...called 'absorbed' or 'grown old': For a person contemplating these things, which are wonderfully produced, is absorbed by their magnitude into the contemplation of the Creator, towards whom, sighing, life seems long and tedious to him, so that he cries out with the prophet: "Woe is me, that my sojourning is prolonged!" And it seems to him to grow too old in these lower things, so that this consideration is appropriately called 'grown old'. The other handmaid is Zilpah, which is interpreted as "gaping mouth", that is, insatiable desire, which indeed arises in dealing with these things: And this is also good, provided that it is subject to Jacob, that is, to the spiritual man. In this house, therefore, which is entirely dedicated to God, and from which the whole church is gathered, our Christ reigns forever. And let these things be said, as far as they pertain to the moral sense.

On the fruits of this house, in which Christ reigns. Chapter VI.

**B**ut let us see what fruits Jacob received from these wives and handmaids. First, it is not without mystery that he had more (children) from Leah than from Rachel, because we expect more from the active life than from the contemplative, and more timely ones, although more lovable ones from the contemplative. Hence, granted that Mary's choice is commended by the Savior as the best, Martha's solicitude is nevertheless not blamed, although it is laborious and experiences many troubles. The best part is also that which presupposes the merit of the active life, and strives to ascend higher: Therefore, Rachel's first son is called Joseph, that is, an increase to all things acquired in the previous life. Hence it is also declared why the latest fruits are from Rachel: because, namely, all the fruits of the active life, through which we are disposed to the contemplative life, are presupposed. This also must not be omitted, that Jacob does not commit adultery with the handmaids, nor do the wives take it ill; indeed, they spontaneously offer the handmaids: because even if a person delights in contemplating and dealing with created things, provided he directs everything to God, he does not sin, but rather merits: Nor does either portion (wife), which seeks God immediately, take it ill, but they spontaneously offer to the husband even the delight in created things, provided they themselves receive the offspring conceived from the handmaids: therefore Rachel said: "I have my handmaid Bilhah; go in to her, that she may bear upon my knees, and I may have sons from her." [Marginal note: Rachel] Which her sister, being jealous, likewise did. But coming to the particular sons, let us begin from the birth from which the spiritual man begins: because fruit is produced much more easily through the active life than through the contemplative life. From her, therefore, are generated first Reuben, then Simeon, Levi, and Judah. Reuben, who is interpreted as "seeing through the middle", signifies holy intention: which directs all things on a straight path to God, so that it does not deviate to the right or to the left. And this intention ought to be the firstborn, [Marginal note: CHRIST] if we desire to produce sons and fruits worthy of eternal life: which the Savior admonishes with a clear voice, saying: "If your eye is simple, your whole body will be luminous," having no part of darkness, but like a lamp of splendor it will illuminate you, looking through the true middle, namely, into

**OF THE SECOND CANTICLE**

the object towards which we strive: For this eye (as all agree) signifies intention: after intention in doing things and observing precepts, obedience to the one commanding follows, so that all things may be accomplished at his nod. Hence, secondly, Simeon is begotten, who is interpreted as 'hearing' and 'obedient'. Levi follows, who is called 'applied,' 'added,' or 'attached': because, having a right intention with readiness to obey, it remains for him to apply his hands to the work. And because in all things we do, we ought to praise God by invoking His name, therefore after these, Judah is born, who is called 'praise' or 'confession' by our people: But the contemplative life, or that higher portion, envied the swift and fruitful offspring of her sister with most holy zeal: And since she did not feel herself so perfect as to be able to bear children, because not yet expiated, she could not fix her eye on God, she offers her handmaid, that is, the contemplation of creatures, through which one comes from the creature of the world to the invisible, and to God: Who conceives and bears Dan, that is, the estimative judgment of the greatness of divine things from these created things which she contemplates: or the judgment by which she most subtly condemns and expiates herself, so that she may be able to strive directly towards God: After whom, Naphtali is immediately conceived and born, who is called 'enlargement of the heart': because from the greatness of created things contemplated by a purified mind, the heart is enlarged, so that it may be able to run towards God: Her sister, emulating this, also offers her handmaid, namely, delight in handling things, which, like a spur and a certain goad, makes our mind eager to accumulate merits. Hence, afterwards, Gad is well produced, who is called 'girt,' namely, for prey and the accumulation of merits, enriched by which merits, and content, she considers herself blessed in a certain way: whence Asher afterwards is born: who signifies 'blessedness': Therefore, joyful and pleasant, she is still animated to offspring, which twin offspring Issachar and Zebulun she again receives: Of whom one is interpreted as 'remembering the Lord', the other 'dwelling of strength': and this indicates that the perfect active life, enriched with merits and with the work completed, arranges the house of the mind with the most beautiful adornment, so that it may be able to receive the heavenly guest, of whom, always mindful, it may be free for God Himself through contemplation. Our Jacob, therefore, resting after the works received from Leah, which pertain to the active life itself and to the contemplative preliminaries, it remains for him to attend only to Rachel and to perfect contemplation: from whom he first begets Joseph, who is called 'increase,' namely, for all the works and merits which he received from Leah and from both handmaids. Therefore (if I am not mistaken) this is the best part, not only because it is more secure and more pleasant, but because it presupposes every merit of the active life and seeks increase: Therefore he loves this offspring more than the others, because he is augmented by all, and because he begot him in optimal rest. Nor is it devoid of mystery that Rachel was prepared for this offspring by mandrakes: which Leah's firstborn, Reuben, had offered to her, whom we declared above to signify intention: for the same intention which was prior in the fruits of the active life, the same also in the progress and fructification of the contemplative-

Therefore, once the first son, heavenly contemplation and taste, has been obtained and added to all merits already acquired, another is also generated, who was Benjamin, and is interpreted as 'son of the right hand,' signifying no other than Him who sits at the right hand of God, Jesus Christ our Redeemer: whom all perfect ones ought to generate in mind and in their innermost being; after whom, as the last offspring, they should cease to give birth. This also must be noted, that in his birth Rachel dies, that is, that superior and divine portion communicated to us, because, already united with Christ himself generated in the mind, our spiritual man, yielding to Him along with Paul, ought to say: 'I live, yet not I, but Christ lives in me.' [Marginal note: Paul] For to Him, the most full and perfect, that portion which is in part yields, and dies, so that it may live in the whole. Therefore, Rachel having died in the birth of this Benjamin, she is buried in Ephrath, between Jerusalem and Bethlehem, that is, in abundance and heavenly riches, for thus Ephrath is interpreted: Which is said to be placed not without mystery between Jerusalem, which is the 'vision of peace,' and Bethlehem, which signifies the 'house of bread': For he who dies to the world and to the animal man, or he who dies by the death of a kiss, which occurs in an ecstasy of the mind (as we have explained elsewhere), is buried in the most abundant riches, which are given to all who call upon Him, and are placed between the vision of true and supernal peace, and that bread of life, which he who eats lives forever: For then he has the beginning of the beatific vision and eternal life; to which the true Jacob and true Israelite desires to ascend, who conceives and brings forth those twelve fruits explained and described by John in his most sacred revelation, where he says: 'In the midst of its street,' that is, in the heart of the true Israelite, 'and on either side of the river,' that is, from both portions, 'is the tree of life,' namely Christ, or His spirit or grace, vivifying us and making us fruitful with twelve fruits produced each month, that is, through individual monthly and lunar revolutions, which are contained under one solar revolution. TONE SEVEN. 305

Yet the most just Prince, indeed the fount of all righteousness, disposes all things in order: he could indeed give paradise without merits, nevertheless he decreed to reward soldiers according to the excellent deeds of each: Likewise, he could remit the injury inflicted upon him by enemies and deserters without any penance, yet he commanded that everyone sinning should be subject to the law of penance, according to the gravity of the offense: He could also, with a mere nod, bestow empire upon his son, and dominion over the universe: yet he did not do this, but rather ordained that he should acquire dominion for himself by hereditary and martial right, and possess it most peacefully after the enemies were vanquished and put to flight: since he is the firstborn of him who created all things: Hence the magnanimous Emperor challenged the most monstrous tyrant of the human race and prince of the world to single combat, whom he also vanquished with fortunate outcome in combat: and with blood flowing from his own noble wounds, he washed away all human defilement, and restored to their pristine liberty those unjustly oppressed by the worst tyrant, and by this supreme generosity bound the human race to himself: Hence it is said: It was necessary for Christ to suffer, [Marginal note: CHRIST] namely for freeing captives, and thus to enter into his glory: Of which glory, dominion and sovereignty over all things is a part. By a similar path, he also led his chosen princes, whom he sent into the whole world to preach the gospel to every creature, and to each he assigned a part of the worldly family, so that by preaching and teaching them, and even expending blood in testimony of doctrine, he might deservedly preside over the tribe or family or nation which he acquired, as sons, and in a certain way redeemed (yet by the power of the supreme redeemer). And these are the true twelve tribes, over which the Emperor and Redeemer promised the Apostles presidency and judgment of the universe: Of which tribes, those twelve Israelite ones were a small image and figure: and both families were distributed by the number twelve: The Apostolic, so that it might pursue in due order the twelve parts of the world corresponding to the twelve signs: That Israelite one, indeed, so that it might prefigure the twelve-fold family of the church with the same number. And both were most excellently divided by that primary growing number twelve, just as all growing things (as we touched upon above) are numbered. For that typical nation grew immensely in a very short time, so much so that it first filled Egypt, then that promised land, which bore the likeness of the holy church: And the twelve tribes, taught and acquired by the Apostles, grew so that in a short time they filled the whole world with believers. Thus, both families were and are augmented, so as to equal the spaces of that immense land about which the prophet sings: "I believe that I shall see the good things of the Lord in the land of the living." [Marginal note: David] To which entry is made through twelve gates guarded by twelve angels: which is built upon twelve foundations: just as the visible heaven itself is divided into twelve signs full of innumerable stars, just as in each twelve-fold family there were innumerable elect beyond the twelve thousand sealed.

How great a harmony those Apostolic tribes may have been distributed according to the division of the figurative family and the signs of the star-bearing heaven.

[Illuminated initial I containing a small landscape scene] That mystery of sacred things must also be observed, that the number twelve is born from four trigons, or from three quaternions, and is divided as a solid into four angles: which is found to be observed in both this family and the heaven of stars. For the beloved Apostle of Christ, speaking of that heavenly division and the true dwelling of the chosen tribes, says: "From the east, three gates; from the west, three gates; from the north, three gates." In imitation of which, the temple was made, through any three gates of which three tribes were accustomed to enter, as we find in the records of the Hebrews. In this same order and sacred arrangement, the children of Israel encamped, by the Lord's command: to the east, three tribes; to the south, three tribes; to the west, three tribes; and to the north, three tribes. This heavenly family follows the order of the heavens, concerning which Astronomers say that to the east are assigned three signs or images; to the south, three images; to the west, three images; and to the north, three images. Moreover, in the regions subject to the first three images, and the eastern ones, three Apostles preached: Simon, Bartholomew, and Matthew. And in the regions directed by the three southern figures, three other Apostles preached: Thaddeus, Andrew, and Thomas. But in the regions of the three western images, James the Less, John, and Philip preached. Indeed, the regions directed by the northern images were entrusted to James the Greater, Peter, and Matthias. These things could suffice for describing their agreement, by being silent (as Plato commands) about particulars; nevertheless, inasmuch as the Lord has enlightened our eyes, we shall attempt to run through certain particulars. If we shall have accomplished these things with full harmony, let glory be rendered to the supreme harmonizer; but if we shall have said less, let the readers please excuse our weakness, which is not even troubled if the supreme Lord has hidden some things from his unworthy servants, which he reserves to be communicated to his chosen friends. Therefore, relying on the grace of Him from whom comes every good, we shall also undertake explaining the agreement of certain particulars, under which prince each tribe truly serves, and through which gate, with Him as leader, it can enter the heavenly kingdom, which it hopes to obtain through continuous and faithful service. And so that we may do this, it must first be seen with what aspect, and in what region of the sky each typical tribe, and with what mystery, it has encamped. Afterwards, we deem it necessary to see into which trigons the heaven is distributed, and to which trigon, or to which sign, each region is dedicated. For it is said that to the east Judah shall pitch his tents by the companies of his army: the prince Nahason son of Aminadab: the number of fighters seventy-four thousand six hundred. Therefore, for this (church) and for its sheep that had perished, the Savior says he came: Who did not change, but perfected, united, and led the family and the house itself to a better lot: Thus also the leaders of this family ruled it more felicitously than the leaders of that figurative house: But both with the greatest concord: about which we will immediately discuss (God leading and favoring).

**On the concordance of the Apostles with the celestial signs. Chapter XII.**

[Decorative initial E] And since not without mystery each region, subjected to its own sign, has been assigned to one Apostle, from this point I deem it necessary to traverse the concordance that each Apostle has with the sign of the region assigned to him: and so that we may do this, the proper names of the Apostles must be seen, as I have been able to extract them from the most recondite monuments of the Hebrews: which names agree with the names found in דברי הימים, that is, in the words of days.

And these names are: First, of the prince of the Apostles himself, שמעון הכפי Simehon hacephi, who by us is called Simeon Peter: for Simehon is interpreted as 'you will hear' or 'obedient'; hacephi, however, is 'rock', and not 'head', as some deceived ones assert: for it is not a Greek word, but a Syriac one signifying 'rock'. The name of the second Apostle is אלעזי Aleuzi, that is, 'God is my strength': for whom we have Andrew, who is interpreted as 'responding to fodder'. The third is James the Greater, who by his proper name is called יעקבאב Iabacobab, that is, 'oppressing': but with letters inverted, in the Hebrew manner, saying כבע cabab, it signifies 'helmet' or 'helmeted'. The name of the fourth is פוליפוס Polipos, that is, 'humble mouth' or 'humiliation of the mouth': for whom we have Philip. The fifth is ברכיה Barachiab, that is, 'blessed by the Lord': for whom I do not know how we have Bartholomew, whom they interpret as 'son of him who suspends the waters': for 'Bar' is a Chaldean rather than a Hebrew word, and Bartholomew is never found in Hebrew names. The sixth is יוחנה Iochana, whom we call John, and it is interpreted as 'grace of God'. The seventh is תמי Tammi, who is Thomas, and it signifies 'twin' or 'didymus'. The eighth is מדון Medon, i.e., 'judging' or 'discerning': for whom we have Matthew, whom some interpret as 'given', believing that name descends from the word נתן natan, which means 'he gave' or 'he donated'. The ninth is James, son of Alphaeus, or James the Less, who is properly called יעקב Iahacob, which signifies 'supplanter', or 'tracker', or 'imitator of footsteps'. The tenth is Thaddaeus, who by his proper name is called חטיפא Chatepha, that is, 'compressing' or 'inflicting violence', and not from תודה Todah, which is interpreted as 'praise'. The eleventh is Simon the Cananaean, who by his proper name is called סמם Samam, which is said to be interpreted as 'name of the mother' or 'destroying them'. The twelfth is מתניה Matan ia, that is, 'given by God', who perhaps (by God's command) was chosen in the place of the betrayer.

However, pursuing the order of encampment, and the concordance of the Apostolic families with the Israelite tribes, and the aspects of the heavens, to which they were encamped, we will begin with Sa- [Marginal note: Simeon] mam, to whom the image of the Twins, of double interpretation, has been attributed: And the 'name of the mother' suits him well: because (as I found in some most recondite monuments) he frequently invoked the name of the supreme mother, the Virgin Mary, by whose favor he destroyed the enemies of Christ and the Church: whom the Church, emulating, supplicantly [Marginal note: Church] says: 'Give me strength against your enemies.' On the harmony of the blessings which Jacob gave to his twelve sons with the twelve peoples to whom the twelve Apostles preached, according to the order of the signs to which they correspond. Chapter XIV.

[Decorative initial I] Now we have somewhat explained the harmony of both tribes, namely, the figurative and the apostolic family with the celestial signs: Now let us see how aptly the father of both families, Israel, prophesied concerning both at the end of his life, who said concerning Reuben: [Marginal note: Israel.] Reuben my firstborn, you are my strength, and the beginning of my sorrow, or of my virility: first in gifts, and greater in power: Or as the literal truth has it: The residue of a gift, or of swelling, and the residue of strength: You are poured out like water, you shall not grow, because you ascended your father's bed, and defiled his couch: Which oracle is for the most part quite clear: For he was the firstborn, and the beginning of the fruit of paternal virility: He also defiled his father's bed, because he mingled himself with Bilhah, his father's concubine, Rachel's handmaid, as is found in Genesis: [Marginal note: Geness.] Therefore he made himself utterly unworthy of celestial influence: hence the father said: That which was prepared for you, namely, shall not descend upon you, because you placed an obstacle, defiling the paternal chamber: Whence it follows: The residue of the gift, and the residue of strength, which was due to you by reason of primogeniture, I do not give: For you are poured out like water, therefore nothing remains that I might give you: For which we have, You shall not grow: and the reason is, because you placed an obstacle, defiling your father's bed, and polluting the way, or course of ascent. What is said here about Reuben, along with what will be said about the other sons, or tribes, has a place in the family begotten by Christ the Father, [Marginal note: CHRI- / STVS.] of whom Jacob was a type. Hence He, as the true father and redeemer of the true Israelite family, said: I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel. Concerning which true and figurative house, rather than concerning the one figuring it, the ancient father Jacob, about to depart shortly to his ancestors, full of the Holy Spirit, said to his sons, האספו (beazephu). Which does not mean 'gather yourselves', as a faulty translation has it, but 'increase', and 'grow in merits and light', so that you may be able to grasp those profound mysteries, which I wish to prophesy will come to you in the last time, that is, in the final age, when the Messiah will come. Afterwards follows הקבצו (hicabzu), that is, 'join yourselves', not only you who are of my stock, but all who ought to participate, or serve under God in both families: Hence he notably said: Hear, sons of Jacob, that is, you who have proceeded from my loins, and who are to proceed: And again he said: Hear, sons of Israel, that is, all who are to serve under God: For from afar, following the footsteps of truth, I am Jacob, but familiar with God, and obtaining true principality from Him for my latest sons, concerning whom it was said: You shall make them princes over all the earth. I am called Israel, foretelling those things which are to come to those better sons, and to the princes of a better family, who are born for their fathers, and constituted princes of the true

**OF THE SECOND CANTICLE**

family for those who were in the figurative. Therefore, to this figurative family I say, "Reuben my firstborn:" For this word is directed to the people responding to the first celestial sign, which is Aries, or to the angelic or divine power presiding over it: This people inhabits Judea, Idumaea, hollow Syria, E- [Marginal note: Hebrews.] gypt (as the Hebrews assert), Britain, Gaul, and Germany. Indeed, the Jewish people (to begin with the former) are called the son of vision, since almost all vision and prophecy was given to the Hebrew people: who was also adorned with the privilege of primogeniture [Marginal note: Exodus.] by the testimony of God, who says in Exodus: "Israel is my firstborn:" Whose chief and royal Tribe was Judah: whence sometimes "Jew" [Marginal note: Paul] is taken for the whole Israelite family, according to that of Paul: "to the Jew first, and also to the Greek." "You are my strength, and the beginning of my virility:" Which is verified to the letter concerning both the figurative and the true family: For the highest Father God showed the first and chief signs of excellent virtue and strength by leading His firstborn out of Egypt, and in the new family He performed the first miracles and signs in Judea and the surrounding region: Nor was He absent from Egypt, in which He spent the first years. In Gaul also He so poured out His strength that its King was adorned with the name of Most Christian, and holds a special protection for the Father in the study of letters and arms. And Germany elects an Emperor, who bears the chief insignia of principality to protect the family of Christ and God the Father. But concerning the Jewish people, what follows is verified: "The residue of the gift, and the residue of strength, which was owed to you as firstborn, I cannot give, so your evil merits demand it:" for you have defiled the bed and the honor of your Father, falsely accusing Him, bringing very many reproaches and injuries, finally conspiring with the greatest wickedness for His death: "Therefore you are poured out like water:" For if water is poured out, less remains in the vessel than from any other liquid: Hence the Jewish people are well compared to poured-out water, because all charisms were immediately emptied from them: For the Jerusalem church quickly failed, and that which was in all Judea, so that nothing of Christianity was left there, except only names, and some memory of the places in which those most revered first fruits of Christianity were celebrated: to visit which some people gather even in our time. Therefore, a tiny spark of Christianity still lives in that region, so that the Mosaic oracle may have its place: "Let Reuben live, and not die, and let him be small in number," because the place of Judea is small, and the worship of God there is small.

But why this was done in both families with their own reasons and sacraments, many things would have to be said, which perhaps would lead us further than the present business requires: But lest it be believed that this was done by chance, or without reason, we will assign

--- Page 765 ---
**SECOND CANTICLE**

at least the reason why Moses, while blessing the tribes, omitted Simeon, as if he had forgotten him, in whose place he put Joseph's son Manasseh, who is interpreted as "forgetfulness." For in this he was in agreement with Jacob, who, coming to Simeon, said: "Simeon and Levi, vessels of warring iniquity." These indeed had received robust strength from an exalted power, but because they abused it against the Shechemites and against their brother Joseph, hence the wise father, and full of God, not only declared that he did not agree with their counsel and fury, but cursed, saying: "Cursed be their fury, because it is stubborn; and their indignation, because it is harsh; because in their fury they killed a man," namely Hamor, "and Shechem his son with his people." But in heart and will they killed Joseph their brother; and in their will they undermined, or tore down, a wall, namely that of the Shechemites, or a bull. For שור (Sor) means both wall and bull. If therefore it is taken for a bull, it speaks of Joseph, of whom Moses says: "His beauty is like that of a firstborn bull." And lest such robust fury, gathered in those two tribes, should cause harm, the divine Patriarch continues: "I will divide them in Jacob, and scatter them in Israel." And so the tribe of Levi was divided, which served the tabernacle for all the tribes, and were sustained by the tithes offered by them. He also did not bless Simeon, because he was not capable of blessing, nor did Moses, or Joshua his minister, assign boundaries to him when the promised land was divided, but placed him within the boundaries of Judah, so that his harsh indignation might be suppressed by Judah's good and abundant influence, and that he might become capable of some good influence from his association. But Levi, whom Jacob did not want to bless, was blessed by Moses: because he redeemed the curse given to him, and earned a blessing from the greatest zeal of divine love, which he showed against idolaters and calf-worshippers, as we read in Exodus. [Marginal note: Exo.] For Moses, seeing the calf set up in the desert, and the people playing around it, said: "If anyone is for the Lord, let him join me." And all the sons of Levi gathered to him, to whom he said: "Thus says the Lord God of Israel: Let every man put his sword upon his thigh; Go, return from gate to gate through the midst of the camp, and let each man kill his brother, his friend, and his neighbor." And the sons of Levi did according to the word of Moses, and killed on that day about twenty-three thousand men. And Moses said: "Today you have consecrated your hands to the Lord, each one in his son and his brother, that a blessing may be given to you." Behold therefore how they acquired a blessing for themselves: which Phinehas confirmed, when, zealous for the Lord his God, he took a dagger and pierced through the genital members Zimri, son of Salu, leader of the tribe of Simeon, together with Cozbi the Midianite, daughter of the prince of the Midianites, with whom he was lying in injury to the God of Israel, from whom many had turned away, initiated into Baal-peor, and mingled with the Moabites and Midianites: and by the death of one, inflicted with such zeal, the sin of Israel was purged, as we read in the book of Numbers. [Marginal note: Numer.] And just as the blessing was restored to the zealous Levites, of which they had been deprived because of the crime of a violated covenant and fratricide, so to zealous Phinehas was given an everlasting priesthood. But since Simeon by no good deed—

Continuation of the agreement of the blessings of Issachar and Zebulun with their peoples. Chapter XVI.

**I**ssachar, second in encampment with the second sign, which is Taurus, seems to me to be fitting. For the oracle says of him: "Issachar is a strong ass," that is, patient and robust in the study of letters, to which that tribe was dedicated. The ass also savors of I know not what clemency, and of its influx, from which wisdom comes, as the more secret Theologians say. [marginal note: Theologians] But setting aside these more hidden mysteries for the time being, let us pursue the literal meaning. For he who ought to progress in doctrine is required to be robust; therefore, in blessing, he is equated with the ass, and in the celestial signs, with Taurus, the most robust of all beasts of burden. He saw here rest and leisure for study, because it was good, and the land in which that tribe dwelt, without the wandering that merchants and soldiers are accustomed to do, because it was delightful; therefore, he adapted his shoulders to bear the great burden that is in the study of letters. And he became a servant to tribute: For Issachar in a way served the tribe of Zebulun, who, being rich and merchants, provided necessities for those of the tribe of Issachar who were devoted to the study of letters, as the Hebrews assert. Hence Moses said, when he distributed the portion of his blessing: "Rejoice, Zebulun, in your going out," that is, when you travel here and there, bringing goods; "and Issachar in your tents," that is, he will dwell or frequent them, so that he may receive the benefits of life as a reward, just as his name indicates, which is interpreted as "reward." If, however, these words are fitted to the regions directed by Taurus, let us see: For those are the maritime regions of Asia Minor, Persia, Media, Parthia, the Cyclades, Cyprus. In the maritime regions of Asia Minor were the seven churches, to which that most famous and unique prophecy in the New Testament, revealed to John on the island of Patmos, which is now called Chios, was dedicated, as is said at the beginning of that vision: "John to the seven churches which are in Asia: Grace to you and peace from Him who was and who is and who is to come, and from the seven spirits who are before His throne," as if those seven chief spirits held a special care for those churches, which are Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia, and Laodicea, near which cities is the island of Patmos, one of the Cyclades, which is now called Chios, where that divine revelation was made. And in these places, with the surrounding regions, the study of human letters flourished greatly; and many men most famous in doctrine came forth from them. For from Ephesus, Heraclitus, called the Ephesian; from the city of Scepsis, in the conti-

on the continent, situated near Antandrus next to Mytilene, were the Socratic philosophers Erastus and Coriscus, to whom letters from Plato are found to have been sent. There was also Neleus, son of Coriscus, Demetrius the grammarian, and Metodorus. From nearby Pergamum was Galen. There, by the great care of the Attalid kings, a library was established, and in it, by Apellicon, the Aristotelian and Theophrastean books were deposited. For Aristotle left his library and school to Theophrastus; and he was the first of all Greeks to collect books, and he taught the kings of Egypt the arrangement of a library. Theophrastus also handed it over to Neleus; Neleus indeed carried it to Scepsis and gave it to his descendants, indeed to unskilled men, whose negligence caused the books to be damaged by dampness and eaten by moths; but transcribed by Apellicon, they were full of errors, as Strabo reports. [Marginal note: Strabo] Whence by some, Aristotelian and Theophrastean philosophy is judged faulty, and not that pure and chaste philosophy which its authors handed down. But however the matter stands, the first library of Athenian learning, which was the mother of studies, was erected in Pergamum. But from the vicinity of Athens, it was quite consistent with those maritime regions, as they are situated in the region of European Greece; for between those maritime regions and Athens are the Cyclades islands, separated from both only by some stretch of sea, which together with those maritime regions directed from Taurus, agree, and with the studious tribe of Issachar. From Coos we have Hippocrates, and, as some assert for certain, Homer. Among these is also Delos, famous for the temple and oracle of Apollo, whence the ancients received great nourishment for their wisdom. Also towards the west, near Rhodes, is Halicarnassus, famous for its Dionysius; and from Mytilene, Pittacus, one of the seven wise men, emerged. It would be lengthy to recount all the famous men who came forth from those places, and with how much labor their inhabitants dedicated themselves to the study of letters.

But approaching Persia, there was Magic, which is a more secret philosophy, whence came those who first adored Christ. Thence Charundas, most excellent in that doctrine, and Avicenna, as some assert. [Marginal notes: Char. Auicena.] And although their school was devoted to the practice and adornment of riding and archery, they were not lacking in the study of letters in the most recondite matters; whence they were most diligent in sacred things. I omit many other things that could be said about the study that the inhabitants of these regions had, since these few suffice to indicate how neatly the influence of the heavens over them aligns with the influence of the tribe of Issachar, whose study was to apply themselves to humanly acquired doctrine; for that which was divinely revealed was given especially to the Levites.
