On the harmony of the blessing given to Judah with the people directed by the sign corresponding to it. Chapter XVII.

[Decorative initial A] In the southern part, in the second order, Reuben placed his face in the first place, which place, however, is the fourth in the order of encampment. But since, in expounding the paternal blessings, following the order of birth, and imitating the father, we have placed him (Reuben) in the first place, in this fourth order, we will place Judah, born in the fourth place, and blessed in the fourth place, with these words: "Judah, your brothers shall praise you, and honor you, namely as a king:" For to him was given the royal scepter, secretly flourishing in that tribe until David came, publicly exalted in that royal scepter, [Marginal note: CHRIST.] which also lasted in kings, or leaders, until Shiloh, that is, the true Messiah: Who, however, did not abolish the kingdom, but changed it for the better and more happily, promising it to all his true and pious followers, saying: "Come, blessed of my Father, possess the kingdom prepared for you." Since, therefore, this kingdom was in the loins of Judah, together with that king before whom every knee bows, therefore it follows: "The sons of your father shall bow down before you: and with true authority and royal vigor, your hands shall be on the necks of your enemies:" "Judah is a lion's whelp or terror." For גור (Gur) signifies both a whelp and terror: But it is better (as I think) understood here as terror, because it follows what precedes: "Your hands on the necks of your enemies:" and it well suits what follows: "From the prey, my son, you have gone up:" All these things are most especially verified in Christ, of whom John says: "The Lion of the tribe of Judah has conquered." And rightly is Christ from the tribe of יהודה (Yehudah), since this name most aptly suits Christ himself, in whom are the four letters of the great name of God, with the dalet (ד) interposed, which signifies four in number, indicating the quadrangular body which God himself assumed, clothing himself according to Paul.

Concerning the harmony of the other two blessed tribes of this trigone with the signs and peoples corresponding to them. Chapter XVIII.

[Large decorative initial A] The other two tribes are Simeon and Gad: whose oracle (Simeon's) has already been explained to have been rather a curse and a certain division, than a blessing: Hence, empty of office and influence by Moses, full of God, and Joshua, his most pious minister, he was most piously placed in the tribe of Judah, lest, deprived of divine influence and abandoned to himself, he should be utterly or largely overthrown. And since these Simeonites did not have their own borders, nor a full portion of the divided region, they lived (as the Hebrews say) from profit acquired in teaching, asserting that there was no scribe or teacher except from the lineage of Simeon: Which things seem to me to have a place among the peoples and regions subject to Aquarius: which are Arabia, Ethiopia, Sarmatia, Oxiana, Sogdiana, Azania, and Media: For the Arabs have no determined region, but live within the borders of others, although Arabia is threefold: Felix (Happy), Deserta (Desert), and Petrea (Stony), since not all the multitude of that nation is contained within them, which extends from there beyond the Syrians, Phoenicians, Palestinians, and Carthaginians, always passing between maritime peoples and the Persian, Egyptian, or Libyan deserts, through the region of Marmarica and Cyrenaica, up to the borders of Mauretania and the Atlantic Sea, so that in them that oracle may find its place: 'I will divide them in Jacob, and scatter them in Israel', which is understood to figuratively comprehend all the people and number of the elect. But the scattered and divided Arabs are the Hagarites:
[Marginal note: Genesis] of whom the angel of the Lord said to Hagar (as we read in Genesis), speaking of their father, and consequently of the whole family: 'He will be a wild man: he will pitch his tents in the region of his brothers'. Gedrosia, however, or Gerdosia, abounds only in aromatics, especially myrrh and nard. Therefore, all these, having obtained the blessing of Gad, are most excellently equated with him in this particular gift. However, by election and faith, if there is any in them, they are reckoned in the Israelite family.

[Marginal note: Moses.] Moses says: "From the blessings of the Lord, his land, namely, let it be blessed, from the fruits of heaven, and from the dew, and from the hidden abyss, beneath that land, namely, and from the dew, which is the ultimate source of heavenly blessing." He continues the blessing concerning these lower things, saying: "From the fruits of the sun," that is, generated by the sun, "and from the fruits of the moon," that is, produced by the moon (for the sun generates, and the moon brings forth offspring), "and from the top of the eastern mountains, and from the fruits of the hills of the world:" For the mountains of the east, which in Hebrew is called קדם *kedem*, signify the mountains of the upper region, in which the paradise of delight is said to have been planted. But the hills of the world signify these lower ones, concerning whose fruits it follows: "And from the fruits of the earth, and its fullness, and the fertility of sheep, namely:" "The Dweller of Sinai," that is, he who would dwell and give the law on Sinai, "let him bring [these blessings] upon the head of Joseph, and upon the crown of his Nazirite," as has recently been explained. "The firstborn of the bull," that is, of that exalted one whom Ezekiel saw to the left of the supreme tribunal, "is his glory or beauty:" "And the horns of the unicorn are his horns:" for with those horns an animal defends itself from attackers: and with these, others are defended from poison: So Joseph was not only defended from the snares of his brothers, but also from the false accusation of Potiphar's wife. He also defended his father and brothers from destruction by a severe famine.

But let us return to Ephraim. He pitched his camp near the fish: Of which image, the regions are Lycia, Lydia, Cilicia, Pamphylia, Phazania or Hazania, as others say, Nazamonitis, and Garamantica. Lycia, and Lydia, and Mysia are inland regions of Asia Minor from Mount Olympus even to Pamphylia, which Cilicia succeeds, indeed opulent and fertile, but with boundaries so confused that ancient memory scarcely remains: For since often different ones have ruled, some have been confused, others utterly overthrown: For after Troy was captured, the Phrygians and Mysians ruled there, then the Lydians, after them the Aeolians and Ionians, then the Persians and Macedonians,

are fertile in fruits, they agree with Ephraim, who is interpreted as 'fruitful'.
Cilicia, however, is famous for Tarsus and Paul: who, although he was of the tribe of Benjamin, was nevertheless in the region corresponding to Ephraim, concerning whom that blessing was given to his father Joseph: 'From there, the shepherd of the stone of Israel:' For Paul was the universal shepherd of the sheep of the stone: who is Christ, and the true foundation of all Israel. The Garamantian region, however, in inner Libya, extends beyond Marmarica as far as Ethiopia, under Egypt as far as Ammon: which is similar [to it] in being palm-bearing and watery: where there are also Nazamones, Psylli, and part of the Getulians: Whose regions are reported to be quite fertile, but in particular not much known to us: because access there for our people is difficult and rare. Manasseh, however, pitched his camp against Cancer: of which image are Bithynia, Phrygia, Colchica, Numidia, Africa, Carthage, and Carchedonia, regions indeed not endowed with greater dignity than the oracle concerning Manasseh bears: for this [tribe] is counted among the twelve tribes as quite fruitful, and itself sharing in the common portion of the blessing.
Nor is anything more singular said about those regions than about this family, concerning which Moses says: 'And these [Marginal note: Moses;]
are the thousands of Manasseh:' Which can indeed be understood in two ways: either because it is a numerous tribe expressed by those thousands: or an influx is denoted, which is from 'aleph', which signifies a thousand, but primarily God himself, from whom all good [comes], [Marginal note: k]
as if to say: 'These are the things which God has granted to you, so that you may live quite abundantly and with a common life among other peoples.' Benjamin held the third place in this trigone against Scorpio, who rules Syria, Commagene, Cappadocia, Metagonite, Mauretania, and Getulia. His blessing, however, given by his father Jacob, was this: 'Benjamin is a ravenous wolf; in the morning he devours the prey, and in the evening he divides the spoil.' But Moses seems to pursue it with a long distance, saying: 'The beloved of the Lord shall dwell in safety by him; he shall dwell between his shoulders all the day long, and he shall rest between his shoulders.' But, as is clear to one who understands well, the words of both agree on the same point: Literally, both prophesied about Saul, the only king from the tribe of Benjamin, for he was like a wolf who secretly seized prey: for he secretly entered into the kingdom, which was due to the tribe of Judah, and he held this from the morning until the evening of his life. And what Jacob says 'from morning until evening,' Moses implies 'throughout the whole day,' when he asserts that he will dwell in the chamber, that is, the royal tribunal: For when the course of his life was completed, the spoil was divided, because the kingdom was transferred to the house of David and to the house of Judah, which had been taken from it, as if prey, during the day of Saul's life: For the kingdom had rested (says Moses), namely in Saul's time, upon his shoulders: [Marginal note: The same;]
Indeed, upon those shoulders, concerning which it is said: 'Saul was taller than any of the people from his shoulders upward.' But let us see what [this means] for the people corresponding to the tribe of Benjamin, and who pitched their camp next to Scorpio: For under this image in Asia is Syria, continuous with Commagene, which receives its borders from Mount Taurus: beyond which, and subsequent Armenia, is Cappadocia directed by the same sign: In Africa, however—

whose peoples in the morning ate that prey, about which it is said: "My son, you have gone up to the prey." **On the agreement of the blessings of the remaining tribes, which are encamped**
**against the fourth trigon, with the peoples directed by it. Chapter XX.**

[Large decorative initial 'I' containing two figures] In the fourth ternary of signs, Dan, Asher, and Naphtali pitched their camps: For Dan agrees with the peoples directed by the Virgin, who are the Greeks, Achaeans, Cretans, Babylonian Mesopotamians, Assyrians, and Elamites: For Greece, extending wider boundaries (as geographers assign) from the Bosphorus to Acarnania, which includes Achaia (which they call Phthia), and also Crete with many adjacent islands. In these regions, the study of letters, acquired by human intellects, flourished. Nor less in the Ba-
[Marginal note: Strabo.] bylonian region, whose beginning from the east is Susa, as Strabo reports, and Pto-
[Marginal note: Ptolem.] lemy shows: It is surrounded by the Euphrates from the north: by Arabia on another side: and is bounded by the Armenians to the north: Which was so fervent in studies, especially mathematical ones, that the Babylonians were even divided into several sects: For some of them, called Chaldeans, professing Genethlialogy, were divided into Orcheni and Borispeni: Of these, the Borispeni are named from the city of Borispa, dedicated to Diana and Apollo. Mesopotamia is situated between the Tigris and the Euphrates, a region indeed most fertile in pastures, contiguous to the Babylonian province, and hence a participant in its doctrine. For here Abraham, easily the chief of all true astronomers, first learned divine astrology from men, but more perfectly through divine illumination.

To whom are contiguous the Assyrians and Elamites, filled with no ordinary wisdom, as is proven in John Damascene, Pherecides Syrus, Bardasanes, Eusebius of Caesarea, and many others: For these were most famous men after the Apostles and Prophets, who were themselves Assyrians: But we do not count these among the wise of doctrine acquired by human ingenuity, since their wisdom far exceeded human wisdom. Therefore, concerning these peoples and princes who were devoted to human wisdom, it can be said what Jacob said about Dan: "Dan shall judge his people, as one of the tribes." [Marginal note: Jacob.] Because, namely, among these peoples there will be wise men for judging. Moses continues the same, [Marginal note: Moses:] although he uses different words: For he says, "Dan is a lion's whelp." Indeed, he himself was not the king of beasts, like Judah, of whom it is written: "The Lion of the tribe of Judah has conquered." But he is called a lion's whelp, as if a king's son: For to no tribe was true kingship given, except to the tribe of Judah; but to the others by a certain participation in that royal inheritance. But what follows from Jacob, when he says: "Dan shall be a serpent by the way, a cerastes in the path, that bites the horse's heels, so that its rider falls backward," all this refers to Samson, who was of the tribe of Dan, indeed a wondrous and astonishing example of strength and fortitude: For he bit the hooves and feet of the horse, that is, the strength of the Philistines, when, having torn out the columns of the palace, by which it was supported as if by certain feet, he caused the princes and more distinguished men of the Philistines who were present there to fall. But since all these things were decreed by God, therefore it follows: "Your salvation," that is, that you may be saved from these falls, or, interpreting "your salvation" as "your strength," you shall await it from the Lord: For which we have: "I will await your salvation, O Lord." Which Moses also explains in other words, saying: "It shall flow," namely, this your strength, "abundantly from Bashan," that is, from that super-worldly richness, from which comes every good gift. Nor are there lacking those who interpret this oracle differently, namely concerning the Antichrist, whom they believe will be born from the tribe of Dan, who will be a heresiarch and a twisted serpent, causing all whom he bites to fall: Whose power will flow from Bashan, that is, from the dryness of grace and the richness of temporal things; for Bashan signifies both. Hence they also believe that this tribe of Dan was omitted by John in the counting of the sealed, lest the origin of such great wickedness be counted among the number of the blessed: For he bites those horses, of which Habakkuk says: "You who ride upon your horses," [Marginal note: Habakkuk.] namely, those restrained by the bit and bridle of true discipline, and by the power of the divine name, about which it is not permitted to speak at present.

To Asher, however, we shall assign Libra, whose regions are Bactriana, Caspiria, Syria, Thebais, Oaxis, and the Troglodytic region. Bactriana is enclosed by the Oxus river in the north and east; to the south, it borders the Arians, with the Caucasus mountains intervening; but to the north, by the Margians and Hyrcanians: and it is fertile in dromedaries and elephants, and quite rich in the abundance of other things: Moreover, it is celebrated for its Phraotes by Philostratus, and for Zoroaster by very many. Caspiria is not far from Bactriana, famous for its mountain and the Caspian Sea: whose inhabitants are exceedingly impious towards their parents, inasmuch as when they reach their seventieth

But let us see how much those things which the oracle relates concerning Asser (Asher) agree with these peoples: For Jacob says:
[Marginal note: Iahac.] Asher, his bread is fat, and he shall yield dainties to kings.
[Marginal note: Moses.] And Moses: Blessed be Asher with children; let him be acceptable to his brethren, and let him dip his foot in oil: his shoes shall be iron and brass; as the days of youth, so also old age. The fatness of food attributed to him refers to those regions which are fertile, and therefore peaceful among their brethren and fellow countrymen. But what is said: His shoes shall be iron and brass, refers to the Caspians, who are said to be cruel and impious towards their parents. But that the days of youth are equated with old age, indicates that those regions have undergone no, or few, changes, but have pursued the same customs through different times: For the same culture, character, and customs have existed among them almost always.

We shall indeed assign Naphtali to Sagittarius: whose regions are Tuscany, Colchis, Spain, and happy Arabia. Tuscany, between the Tyrrhenian Sea and the Tiber river, is filled with many noble and timely fruits, but easily deceptive. The Colchian region is between Iberia and the Euxine Sea, and bounded by the Caucasus mountain: and separated on the northern side by the Corante river from Asiatic Sarmatia: but on the west by the Moschian mountain, and bordering Trapezis: Also, from that part which is opposite the Sarmatian plains, there is a very dense forest of all kinds, especially with trees suitable for building ships. The deserts of another Arabia distinguish Happy Arabia from the north: on the east by the Persian Gulf: on the west by the Arabian (Gulf): on the south by the great sea, which is outside both gulfs: Indeed, it is happy with very many gums and perfumes, and so much opulence, that Alexander the Great was wonderfully delighted by it, as historians recall. But it was happier by the law given on Mount Si
[Marginal note: Paulus] nai, not without mystery, which the Apostle hints at, although he does not explain it, when he says: Sinai is a mountain in Arabia, joined to that which is now Jerusalem, which is our mother: For the words of the Apostle are deeper than they sound in voice.

Spain has the Sardinian Sea to the south, on the west the Atlantic as far as the north, on which side it is indeed wild and harmful: but on the south it is almost entirely most fertile and happy: Let us see if the eulogy of Naphtali suits these regions: For Jacob said: Naphtali is a hind let loose; he gives goodly words. **OF THE SECOND CANTICLE**

**Digression: why no particular tribe or region was assigned to Paul, the most famous apostle. Chapter XXI.**

[Large decorative initial E] And I deem it necessary to consider why it is recorded that no tribe, no family, or church, and no region was assigned to Paul, who labored more than others: But this (as I clearly demonstrate) was the reason: because to him was entrusted the care not only of one, but of all churches, as a universal pastor, or a general vessel chosen for the salvation of all nations, as he him-
[Marginal note: Paulus] self, speaking with the Corinthians, says: "My daily pressure, and the solicitude for all the churches." Just as also the royal Prophet, full of the Holy Spirit, sings in a triumphant
[Marginal note: Dauid] song, saying: "In the churches," namely the new ones collected from all tribes, "bless the Lord God from the springs of Israel," indeed from the twelve Apostolic springs, of which the twelve tribes bore the type, and their twelve springs of Elim. But because the figurative springs were going to fail, those representing them are rightly called defective: for Elim is interpreted as "failing." But the true and figurative springs by no means fail, but (the highest Truth bearing witness) from them flows water, and living springs gushing forth into eternal life, and continuously irrigating the regions entrusted to them. Therefore Peter was a spring, James was a spring, John was a spring; finally, all the Apostles were springs, each one irrigating his own family: But Paul, the most abundant spring of all, irrigated all. Hence follows the Prophet: "There," that is, in all those churches, "Benjamin, a young man in an ecstasy of mind," and caught up even to the third heaven, "and those lofty breasts, from which he drew milk and water, which he might offer to all the churches." Therefore all interpret this Benjamin as Paul, who was also descended from his family, and because what the oracle brings forth is verified concerning him word for word:
[Marginal note: Iahac.] for the patriarch Jacob says: "Benjamin is a ravenous wolf; in the morning he shall seize the prey, and in the evening he shall divide the spoils." He was indeed a plunderer in the beginning of his life, when he persecuted the church of God: but in the evening, growing old, he so divided
[Marginal note: Paulus] the food and spoils, that he said: "I have become all things to all people, that I might gain them for Christ." I also deem it necessary to observe the twofold name, suitable for both: For that last son of our Patriarch Jacob was first called Benoni, that is, "son of my sorrow," because his mother bore him in extreme sorrow: Afterwards by his father, he was named Benjamin, that is, "son of the right hand." Paul was no different, who at first was a son of sorrow to the church, while he fiercely persecuted it even to its utter destruction, if it had been permitted to him from above: But admonished by the voice of Christ, he was changed into another man, and became a true son of the right hand, while he, calling upon Him whose pro-
[Marginal note: idem.] per seat is at the right hand of God the Father, received Him with all his strength in the innermost parts of his heart, so that he no longer lived for himself, but rather for his guest, saying: "I live, yet not I, but Christ lives in me." Nor did he then speak from himself, since
[Marginal note: idem.] Christ suggested the words to him, as he testifies elsewhere: "Do you seek proof of Christ who speaks in me?" Hence, not without mystery, Paul, now made a son of the right hand,
[Marginal note: Horati.] not only by painters, to whom, along with poets, "they dare anything"

--- Page 782 ---
TOMVS SEPTIMVS. 321

to him there was always equal power, but also in the seals of apostolic diplomas he is placed at the right hand of Peter. Nor do I think it should be supposed that blessed Sylvester and those ancient fathers, who were entirely vigilant in ecclesiastical discipline, allowed this order of such great princes to be by chance or without deliberation in the apostolic seals, but full of God, contemplating sacred mysteries, they intentionally placed him at the right hand who fought the wars of the Prince's right hand, who is Christ JESUS: And he was a very strenuous soldier, and laboring above all others, he enrolled countless fellow soldiers for his Emperor, whom he had gathered from diverse peoples, nations, and tribes: whence he was also called "doctor of the Gentiles" by the supreme Emperor: For he preached, as he himself says, the gospel of Christ where Christ was least named, as it is written: "Because those to whom it has not been announced concerning him, shall see: and those who have not heard [Marginal note: Isaiah.] concerning him, shall understand." Therefore, to carry the gospel to the Gentiles, he went to the Arabs, Greeks, Italians, Spaniards, and regions of diverse peoples, traversing a great part of the world, and finally with Peter, the prince of the apostles, he undertook the care of the universal church, favoring it by the power of the right hand of the divine word, just as Peter sustained it with the left hand of the judgment entrusted to him. Hence, the former is adorned with the sword of the spirit, which is the word of God, while the latter is adorned with the keys of judgment, noble emblems: And embraced on both sides, they followed Christ, who always held the middle ground in the ecclesiastical kingdom, although coming forth from the Father's right hand, he returned there again: And because they were embraced in their pilgrimage, and together killed for Christ, they also reign together. There therefore Benjamin, in an ecstasy of mind, because elevated to heavenly things, he saw the secrets of God, which it is not lawful for a man to speak. And with this illustrious master of the army, not without mystery, are enumerated the princes of Judah, the princes of Zebulun, the princes of Naphtali, so that through these may be understood all princes and soldiers who fight against all kinds of troops of our enemies, which are reduced to a threefold battle line by John and by our wise men: For the prince of the army of faith and due submission against the battle line of pride is sung as Judah, who, interpreted as praise and confession, rules those who, confessing God with heart and mouth, acknowledge Him as Lord and teacher of all good things. But the prince of the troop of hope is called Zebulun, who signifies a dwelling place of fortitude, in which soldiers gathered and fortified by the protection of hope least fear the harshness and horror of war. But the prince of charity is Naphtali, who signifies dilatation, or more truly (as we touched upon above) equalization: for charity dilates the heart and all things, and equalizes all things: And this troop is raised against avarice, hatred, factions, and all things inimical to true peace, just as the bulwarks of hope are against enervating and soft wantonness. Therefore, under the great and distinguished leader Paul, and the supreme Emperor Christ, we all, a threefold troop, fight against the three-headed enemy, and that immense and dire Cerberus: Therefore, to Paul, as master of the entire army, not a particular but a universal church is assigned, just as to Peter, constituted judge by the supreme Prince, all jurisdiction of the Christian Commonwealth is entrusted.

**SECOND CANTICLE**

What is signified by that intervening five-fold company in the encampment around the tabernacle of the covenant. Chapter 22.

[Marginal note: Numbers.]
**T**herefore, the encampment having been arranged around the tabernacle of the covenant or of summons, where the people were summoned to the divine oracle, we read in the Book of Numbers that five tents were placed between the tabernacle and those twelve tribes surrounding it: Of these, two belonged to Moses and Aaron, concerning whom it is said in the same place: "They shall encamp before the tabernacle of the covenant," that is, on the eastern side, Moses and Aaron with their sons, having custody of the sanctuary in the midst of the sons of Israel, so that whoever, being a stranger, approaches, shall die. Also, three other tents of the sons of Levi are commanded [to be placed] by three families, which are: the Kohathites to the south, the Merarites to the north, the Gershonites to the west: And all these with their assigned duties: over the chiefs of all of whom was Eleazar, son of Aaron. But the leader of the Kohathites was Elizaphan, and they took care of the vessels, namely, the table, mortars, bowls, candelabra, lamps, oil vessels: fire pans, flesh-hooks, tridents, hooks, pitchers, and such like: Moreover, also oil for preparing the lamps, and incense, and sacrifices. The Gershonites, whose leader was Eliasaph, guarded the curtains of the tabernacle, the roof, and the other covering, and especially the blue veil of the tent, which hung in the vestibule of the tabernacle of the covenant: Also the curtains of the court, and the veil that was before the tabernacle itself: as well as the cords, the vessels of ministry, and all things that pertained to the altar. But the Merarites, whose leader was Suriel, took charge of the assigned boards, the bars of the tabernacle, the pillars of the court all around with their bases, pegs, and ropes, and all the altar's furniture, just as the Gershonites [were responsible for] those things that pertained to erecting the altar itself: And they were chosen from the thirtieth year of age up to the fiftieth.

Which tabernacle, without doubt, prefigured that true tabernacle not made with hands, just as the Apostle, discoursing with the Hebrews, continues at length, saying:
[Marginal note: Paul.]
"For the first tabernacle was made, in which were the candelabra, the table, the showbread, which are called holy: But behind the second veil was the tabernacle, which is called the Holy of Holies, having a golden censer, and the ark of the covenant covered all around with gold: in which was a golden urn having manna, and Aaron's rod, which had budded, and the tablets of the covenant: above which were the Cherubim of glory overshadowing the mercy seat, concerning which it is not necessary to speak in detail. But these things having been thus arranged, into the first tabernacle indeed the priests always entered, completing the offices of sacrifices, but into the latter only the High Priest, not without blood, which he would offer for his own and the whole people's ignorance: the Holy Spirit signifying this, that the way into the holiest was not yet made manifest, while the first tabernacle still had its standing. Which is a parable for the present time, according to which gifts and sacrifices were offered, which could not make perfect..."

--- Page 784 ---
**TONVS SEPTIMVS.** [Page number:] **322**

...which could not perfect the conscience of the worshiper, being concerned only with foods, drinks, and various washings, and carnal ordinances, imposed until the time of correction. But Christ, having come as High Priest of the good things to come, through a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made by human hands (that is, not of this creation), nor through the blood of goats or calves, but through His own blood, entered once for all into the holy places, having obtained eternal redemption. To discuss this tabernacle in detail will perhaps be considered rash, and rightly so, since the Apostle did not dare to do it; or he was unwilling, because he did not have initiated and perfect disciples to whom he might reveal the secrets of wisdom. But since it is given to us to behold the glory of the Lord with unveiled face, we shall consider it by no means rash to at least sketch something of this kind (with the Holy Spirit as guide). Therefore, that typical tabernacle was in the midst of the camps and figurative tribes, signifying the true tabernacle not made by human hands, that is, not of this creation, but produced by a more blessed generation, which is Christ Jesus, erected in the midst of the true tribes and camps of this entire universe, according to that prophetic saying: "He has worked salvation in the midst of the earth." For Jerusalem, where propitiation was found, is in the middle of the world, near the supercelestial temple, as more recondite theologians assert. And it is (if we follow the astronomers) in the angle of the southern triangle, near that true south, of which Habakkuk says: "God will come from the south." [Marginal note:] Abacuc. To which region God is also said to have walked when He wished to succor the first parent and cover his sin with a garment of skins made from the hide of that Lamb who bore the sins of the world: For from that region He bestowed all gifts of grace upon us: for there He was born, there He taught, there He suffered, and there He rose, and from there He ascended to that true south and supernal temple, from where He gave gifts to men, and from where all mercy, grace, and salvation [come]: According to which all companies and camps ought to direct their banner and their face, so that their countenance and prayer may be directed there, from where benefits are hoped to be received: Therefore, this tabernacle was erected in the middle of both worlds, so that He who is said to hold the middle on the supramundane throne may reign everywhere in the house of Jacob: and here below He took possession of the middle of the habitable earth. Thus also Christ, the true tabernacle, just as He always held the middle in being born, teaching, appearing, and dying, so reigning in the midst of the house of Jacob, He sits as the true Israel, that is, the heir or prince of God. Therefore, to this true heir and prince of God, who conquered the principality of the world with the trophy of the cross erected in the middle of the world, all tribes and families serving God look, drawn into that sacred dodecad (twelve), three for each part of heaven: for each of which (as John testifies) [Marginal note:] Iohan. three gates lie open to the heavenly kingdom. Very beautifully and most mysteriously also, that typical tabernacle is described as bipartite, so that it might signify the true biform tabernacle: where human nature is found first, and

CHRIST himself is called holy, because he was anointed with the holy oil of divinity above all his princes, and illuminated by the light of that lampstand, which says: "I am the light of the world." And there are also found the showbread, Christ also affirming this, for he says: "He will go in and go out, and everywhere he will find pasture." For Christ himself, as man, is the true prince of faces, through whom we are introduced to the face of divinity. Therefore, into these holy places, all who sacrifice and meditate enter at will, because the meditation of man and his work is easy. But into the Holy of Holies (which is the divine nature enclosed in the human, from which propitiation and salvation are properly expected), the great priest, and not a common one, enters; because only one who is perfect, and who has consecrated himself most excellently to God, enters the divine inner sanctum. He enters indeed once a year, when, renewed and transformed for the better, he gathers new and annual fruits, as if a well-cultivated other world; and these are always so much better, the more he is separated from subdued flesh and almost extinct blood. Therefore, he is said not to enter without blood, by which, progressing, he is always purified, until, with it completely extinguished, he merits to become a son of God according to the power delivered by the Word. But there is a great difference between the typical and the true tabernacle: for there, the blood of animals only atoned for the ignorance of the priest and the people; but here, in the blood of Christ, all sins are purged, provided they have not been perpetrated against the Holy Spirit, which are forgiven neither in this age nor in the future. And so, entering, he finds the golden censer, that is, the vessel of prayer enriched by perfect charity. There, the ark of the covenant, namely, perfect understanding of scripture, which is given to true priests, and to those who, well purified, have attained understanding and merit to see God. They also receive that most sweet and hidden manna, which no one knows except he who receives it. Moreover, he finds the rod, that is, the priestly virtue blossoming and always progressing for the better. He also beholds the tablets of the covenant inscribed by the finger of God at will, because he finds engraved in his heart the love of God and of his neighbor, to which, as to two principal engravings, the whole law and the prophets are reduced. Finally, there he beholds the cherubim of glory, through whom shine (as we touched upon above) all created things, bipartite into a celestial and terrestrial structure, above which sits he from whom all propitiation emanates. But between this tabernacle and the twelve tribes surrounding it, which comprise the entire host of God's soldiers, five particular and separate companies are said to lie between, not without mystery, in as many tents: Which (to set aside the anagogical sense for now) in the Church of God (if I am not mistaken) signify five approved ranks of priests, leaders, Levites, and mediators between God himself, who was said to reside in the tabernacle, and the people of God gathered and described by those twelve companies. And these are the colleges of Peter, Augustine, Benedict, Basil, and Francis, to which all other companies of particular ministers of God are reduced, or from them as from prin-

But the three following, the multitude of Levites, who are the Kohathites, Merarites, and Gershonites, signify three other assemblies of regulated (orders): For the Kohathites, who are interpreted as "those who grieve," represent the troops of Benedict, who, obscure and always squalid, seem dedicated to continuous mourning for sins and the death of Christ: Hence to them were entrusted mortars, that is, vessels in which sins are crushed, censers for the fumigation of prayers, and bowls, by which heavenly things are tasted: Moreover, candelabra, and lamps of readings, and of heavenly lights: Also vessels of the oil of mercy, by which they always pity others, and receptacles of fires, and of the flames of the Holy Spirit. Also small forks, tridents, hooks, shovels, and such things, by which the fire of fervor and love may be stirred up. But all these things were believed to be entrusted to them clothed in hyacinthine and celestial color, since they ought always to be intent on heavenly things by continuous contemplation, in act or in virtue, so that they may observe that evangelical saying: "One ought always to pray, and never give up." [Marginal note: CHRI-] The Merarites, who signify "those who are embittered" or "those who cover watches," represent the family of Basil and the Anchorites, who, with a certain most severe austerity in solitary life, intent on continuous vigils, made themselves hard and bitter to themselves, so that they might be an example of evangelical mourning to others: To whom, deservedly, as to most robust men, all the strong things were entrusted: columns, bases, bars, planks, and such monuments of the tabernacle: But alas, it is to be lamented, it is no wonder if we have seen the tabernacle for the most part ruined, because it has neither Pauls, nor Peters, nor Macarii, nor Antonies, nor Hilarions, nor such as these, who might sustain the tabernacle itself with sanctity, doctrine, miracles, and example. [Marginal note: STVS.] But the Gershonites, whom they interpret as "strangers" or "outcasts," represent the poor men of the Gospel, to whom it is commanded that they should lead their lives precisely according to the measure of the Gospel, and be strangers and pilgrims in this world: and live entirely separated and cast out from it, so that they may say with the Apostle: "To me the world has been crucified, and I to the world." To these were entrusted the curtains of the tabernacle, the curtains of the courtyard, the coverings, the roofs, the trials, and all things which pertained to covering the sacred things, so that they might nevertheless reveal and uncover the secrets at the time appointed by the Supreme Father. Meanwhile, some have preceded these, who have given forth certain flashes of the immense light hidden in the tabernacle, as can be clear to those who have read the Scotists, Maronites, Halesians, Ockhamists, Bibracenses, and such like. To them also was committed the hyacinthine and celestial veil.

What the seventy-two disciples signify, whom our prince JESUS is said to have chosen in the Gospel. Chapter XXIII.

[Large decorative initial V containing figures of people]
Beyond the group of twelve and five, about which we have already discussed, those who were privy to divine secrets assert that Christ JESUS, the Lord of all things and nations, chose seventy-two disciples, this indeed, so that both the typical and evangelical family might in part agree with the whole supreme world; nor less with our tabernacle, which itself also bears the image of the world: For in the figurative and legal family, not only the number twelve and five are found, but also seventy-two princes were commanded by the Lord to be chosen, so that it might itself bear a perfect image of heavenly things, where the twelve signs, seventy-two princes, and that sacred quinary are found, to whose goal God acts familiarly with us, and in that very thing denoted by the last letter of the great four-letter name (as more secret theologians assert) the supreme craftsman fashioned the world. But those seventy-two princes are distributed in the heavens in such a way that six are said to preside over each sign, and over seventy-two languages: from which is gathered that very great multitude of the elect, which no one can number. And it is very well gathered from the seventy-two, which number is derived from the first perfect senary and from the first increasing duodenary, so that this family, gathered from every nation that is under heaven, may be understood as perfect and superabundant: which most full sacrament is found more happily than in heaven and in the figurative [family], in the kingdom and family of Christ, to whom all power in heaven and on earth has been given: Which mystical body under Christ, the perfect head, is also perfected with all fullness, just as this natural body, and human tabernacle, is made up of seventy-two joints and as many articulations: of which twelve principal ones are in the arms and legs: For in each arm there are three joints: one at the shoulder blade, a second at the elbow, a third at the hands; which combined yield six. Again three in each leg: one at the thigh, a second at the knee, a third at the ankle; which are indeed as many as in the arms, and when calculated together, constitute twelve. Again three

joints are in each finger of the hands, from which thirty joints result from these ten fingers, and as many in the ten toes of the feet, which all combined together constitute sixty, and together with those twelve major ones, they make seventy-two: Nor should anyone object by that which is commanded in the book of Nu- [Marginal note: Nume.] mbers, that only seventy should be gathered, to whom the spirit of Moses should be imparted: For even there the number seventy-two is found, if those two are counted together, who, filled with the same spirit (as we read there), prophesied in the camp, who therefore were not counted with the others, because (as Rabbi Solomon says) they did not receive a written lot: Or (as it pleases others) Moses and Aaron were counted with those seventy, so that an equal portion of six from [Marginal note: Ra. That Christ rules and governs the whole mystical and worldly body. Chapter XXIII.

**F**ormed therefore, the mystical body itself, from all the elect unto life, as if from great and small members, it is fitting that he who is the life and resurrection of all should vivify his whole body and all its members, just as the particular soul vivifies the body which it informs, and all its members. This also must be observed, that the soul not only vivifies the body, but rules and moderates the whole of it, and all its parts: No less is Christ the moderator and ruler of his body: Therefore [Marginal note: Paulus.] Paul calls him not only life, but also the head of this catholic body, saying to the Colossians: He is the head of the body of the church. Nor is he only the ruler of this mystical body, but also of the whole worldly body, just as it itself was fashioned through the word that lies hidden in Christ, so that he may protest [Marginal note: CHRI STVS.] and say not without cause: All power has been given to me in heaven and on earth: It was certainly given [Marginal note: Sapien.] by him, to whom it is said in the book of Wisdom: But you, Father, govern all things from the beginning by your providence. Moreover, diligently how He preserves what He has built. Why then should anyone think that God, in creating living beings and the other parts of the world, did not foresee beforehand where all things were to be placed before they came into being, and does not see how all these same things are preserved in their proper places? Therefore, He who knows all things does not ignore: Nor is He powerless to rule: He who could make all things: Nor does He refuse or disdain to govern those things which He has made, whether they be nobler or viler. Therefore, no doubt about this providence remains for the wise, who know the divine nature to be wise, best, and most powerful. Nor does the governor of the universe himself have providence only by a certain general governance, as some assert, because if he protects and cares for the whole, it is necessary that he also consult for the parts: For nature is so constituted that well-being in the universe cannot exist unless the parts are also rightly disposed: For neither a physician, nor a ship's captain, nor an army general, nor a head of a household, nor a ruler and governor of the Republic, nor any craftsman, whoever he may be, cares in such a way that he manages the more important things and despises the lesser, but each is then considered to perform his duty when he applies himself to individual things with study and diligence, as the nature of each demands. But if men do not even overlook the lesser things, certainly God is not to be thought to neglect even the smallest things, and much less does He despise man, whom He has placed over all living beings. Therefore, He is that supreme Father who knows all things, numbers all things, measures all things, and cares for all things with a special governance: which governance He also committed to the Son as a legitimate heir after the triumph over the tyrant. Therefore, He rules all these same things with wisdom and power handed down from the Father. But many are disturbed by those things which seem to happen out of order, and are not worthy of such great governance: For evils arise everywhere, which ought not to happen under God's rule, since evils cannot come from God, as not only our own people assert, but also Plato shows in the third book of the Republic. [Marginal note: Plato.] And so that we may omit other things which seem to deviate from the order of nature and good governance, we will run through some things concerning the world's overseer, whether he governs badly: For these things have so struck even the wise and principal heroes in God's kingdom, that they seem to break out with a certain impatience even against God himself, the governor. "I will cry out (says Habakkuk) suffering violence, and you will not save? [Marginal note: Abacuc.] Why have you shown me iniquity and toil, to see plunder and injustice against me? Why do you look upon the scorners, and are silent when the wicked trample on one more righteous than himself?" Another point also arises, which particularly pertains to Christ, to whom the power of ruling has been given, and that is: "Since he himself came for the salvation of all, why is his doctrine and redemption rejected by so many? And why does he permit his vineyard to be destroyed by all who pass by the way, and to be devoured by the singular beast and tyrant of this world, whom he already boasts of having cast out?
[Marginal note: CHRIST.] And why did he preach more in Chorazin and Bethsaida than in Tyre and Sidon, when he himself threatens and says: 'Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! Why also does he pour out greater charisms more in one place and nation than in another? And if he can provide for all, why (as he himself foretold) did he permit very many false prophets and false apostles and false Christs to arise and lead many astray?" To these questions, we will answer, saying: "Because just as in a body well regulated by any soul, humors are often altered from diverse causes, and if the powerful virtue of the soul resists them, the body is preserved strong, although it is altered in some part and in some way (for it cannot be that a body subject to alteration and corruption should not be altered); in the same way, in such a great body of the Church, composed of pilgrims still warring and subject to various defects, it cannot be (unless the pilgrims were impeccable, which, as they say, involves a contradiction in terms) that some should not be altered, although the members are vivified by Christ with true and powerful life, and he is the salvation of all the infirm, who does not cease to succor them in their weakness of virtue, those whom he commanded in his stadium

To these members, endowed according to their own virtue, he permits various enemies to attack us with strength, cunning, deceit, ambushes, and importunity, so that the triumph of those who conquer may be more glorious in the power of him of whom it is said: "But thanks be to God, who gives [Marginal note: Paul.] us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ."

The explanation of this through an oracle. Chapter XXV.

<div style="font-size: 200%; float: left; margin-right: 0.1em;">D</div>E this dominion to be given by the Father to our Redeemer Christ, there exists a wonderful and indeed, to those who understand, a very clear oracle, where also the time when it will be given is secretly hinted at: For God speaks to David, the chief father and true type of Christ, saying in the second book of Kings and in the first book of Chronicles: [Marginal note: Kings, Chronicles.] "When your days are fulfilled, and you rest with your fathers, I will raise up your seed after you, which will come forth from your womb, or your intestines"; inasmuch as in Hebrew it has ממעיך *mimeheca*, which means "from your intestines." Therefore it cannot refer to the father, but to the mother, from whose intestines Christ came forth. For a child does not come forth from the intestines, but from the loins and the paternal rod. So therefore, to denote the true king to be born of a woman alone, who was the daughter,

--- Page 793 ---
CANTICLE THE SECOND

And David himself, notably said that seed, from which the true king would be born, would come forth from the intestines. The oracle continues: "And I will establish his kingdom:" Which cannot be understood of Solomon, because while he was still alive, the Lord through Ahijah the Shilonite promised it to the ten tribes of Jeroboam, which He also gave into his dominion. It continues: "He shall build a house for my name:" indeed the true house of Israel, prefigured by that typical one which preceded it. And this is that house of which [Marginal note: Gabriel.] the heavenly messenger to the mother said: "And he shall reign over the house of Jacob forever," as we have explained above. It continues: "And I will establish his throne forever," Behold how clearly this excludes the kingdom of Solomon, which quickly failed. Therefore, it speaks of the kingdom of Him who is King of Kings, and Lord of Lords: Of whom David himself sings in the forty-fourth hymn of the entire alphabetical series, saying under the letter Mem, מלכותך Malcuteca, that is, "Thy kingdom is a kingdom of all ages:"

"I will be to him a father, and he shall be to me a son:" Which cannot be understood except of Him who said through the mouth of the prophet, to whom the promise concerning Him was made. [Marginal note: Psal.] "The Lord said to me, 'You are my son; today I have begotten you.'" How then that [phrase] "When your days are fulfilled" is to be understood, we will explain, as much as the Lord permits. For the days appointed for each person from the beginning (as we have in the more secret Theology of the Hebrews) are a thousand years, to which term, although some approached it, like Adam, Methuselah, and others, none however completed it, due to the exigency of the sin of the protoplast. And from the flood, because of the common sins inflicted upon the human race, the term was contracted to one hundred and twenty [Marginal note: Gene.] years, as we read in Genesis according to the common interpretation, although the oracle hints at something else, nor is it properly verified in this sense, since Abraham lived 175 years, Isaac 180, Jacob 137. But if anyone were to reach the term appointed from the beginning, he would attain to the thousandth year, according to which term the Lord spoke to David: For from the creation of the world until Christ were 3784 years. But from the creation of the world until the death of David were 2880 years. Therefore, from the death of David until Christ were 906 years. As is clear to anyone calculating: Add 70 years of David's life, and it will be 976. Add again the number of the letters of David's name, as it is written in Chronicles, namely with a Yod, thus דויד: For in the books of Kings it is written without a Yod, thus דוד, all these things not without mystery. That name, therefore, thus written, gives 24. Which number, if added to the previous number, makes exactly a thousand: which number is that of a complete age, [Marginal notes: Iohan. Pytha.] as we have said. Nor should anyone wonder if the number of the name is added, because unless some mystery lay hidden there, John would not have said in the Apocalypse: "Let him who has understanding calculate the number of the beast, for it is the number of a man." Pythagoreans also professed to prognosticate many things through the numbers of names. Therefore, to this number twenty-four, which is made up of a double twelve, if the number of years he lived and the years that flowed from his death until Christ are added, the perfect course of a man's life is completed:

--- Page 794 ---
**SEVENTH TONE. 327**

And again, in the calculation of numbers, which resulted from certain words of the oracle, that complete millennium is obtained with the years of the Messiah's life, which words are these: כי ימלאו ימיך ושכבת "When your days are fulfilled, and you lie down (sleep) etc." The calculation of those letters is exactly 1035, which is the number of years from the day of David's conception until the death of Christ: For beyond those thousand years, Christ lived thirty-three and a half (years): And if nine months are taken, during which David was in his mother's womb, and nine months of Christ himself, they give a year and a half: which time, added to those thirty-three and a half years, makes the thirty-fifth. Nor should anyone wonder why Christ, the most perfect of all men, did not reach those thousand years, the full course of human life: For Christ, as the new man, gave a beginning to a new life and new laws: For the first man was from the earth, earthy; the second man from heaven, heavenly, completed a new course of life, which is by no means to be explained here. To which words of the oracle, to pursue our purpose, David, responding to God, full of many mysteries, says: "This is not from my merits, namely, but because it seemed good in your eyes, O Lord God, that you should speak concerning the house of your servant from afar: For this is the law of Adam, O Lord God:" The mysteries of these words are not perceived, except in the Hebrew characters, which are עבדך למרחוק וזאת תורת האדם אדני. The extreme (last) letters of these words are כקתת סי with ל which is a word by itself, the calculated number of which is undoubtedly a thousand. This method of calculating by the last, or first, letters of words is very common among the Hebrews: And with ת (tav) removed from תורת (Torat), there remains תור (Tor), which, when calculated, gives 606. This number is also given by the letters of the name Jesus, & Mary ישו מרים, as is clear to one who knows. And this the true law of man made, that just as through man we had lost all good things, so through man we might recover all good things, according to that of Paul: "For since by man came death, and by man came also the resurrection of the dead."

**EIGHTH TONE. 328**
**CHRIST IN THE MOST HOLY TRINITY**
**is the middle person. Chapter One.**

[Large decorative initial O] All who speak of the Trinity easily agree that the Son, and the Word which was made flesh, and named JESUS, and Christ in Greek, and Messiah in Hebrew, but Anointed in Latin, holds the middle place among the persons of that most holy Trinity: in which the Father is the first root of all emanations, both in divine and in created things: And the Holy Spirit is produced by the Father and the Son, and produces nothing in that most holy Trinity: The Son is also the middle person, produced indeed by the Father, and at the same time producing the Holy Spirit with Him by an eternal emanation: This doctrine is professed not only by all Christians, but also by the more secret Theologians of the Hebrews, who teach that חכמה *hochma*, which signifies wisdom, ema- [Thehe.] nates from the supreme fount, or springs from the super-excellent root, which they call כתר עליון *keterhaliona*; from which two founts, or from the first fount and the light proceeding from it, that third is produced which they call בינה *bina*, which we, properly interpreting, can call prudence or understanding: Indeed, that understanding of which it is said in Ecclesiasticus: "And [Ecclesi.] with the spirit of understanding he will fill him": Understanding is indeed a degree of knowledge more proximate to us than wisdom, which is attributed to the Son: and therefore more easily graspable by us: Therefore the Son said: "I have many things to say to you, [CHRIST.] but you cannot bear them now," because, namely, you are not able to endure the splendor of my wisdom: "But when that spirit of truth comes, he will teach you all things, and will suggest to you all things whatsoever I shall have said to you, at a certain lower degree than these things are to be taught in me": For no one knows the Son, properly speaking, except the Father: But at a certain lower degree, He also offers Himself to us to be seen, according to what He said: "He who loves me will be loved by my Father, and I will love him: And I will manifest myself to him." And sometimes He also manifests the Father through Himself, according to what He says: "He who sees me, sees also my Father," a person indeed more sublime than all of us, since He is therefore more remote from our grasp: The Holy Spirit, however, is more familiar to us: but the Son is the middle between both. And although God is a circle, and a certain intellectual sphere, whose center, that is, everything created, is everywhere, nevertheless, under the aspect of persons, we express them not by a circle, but by number, saying: First, second, and third, or last person, beyond which no production of persons in divine things is given: But in that middle [person], as in a certain house, all things are placed by vital ideas: Whence, just as that middle person was the medium through which all things emanated from the Father, so also it is the medium through which the Father

Christ is the true tree placed in the midst of paradise. [Marginal note: Cap. II.] Chapter II.

[Large decorative initial E] ND so that it may be clearly signified that the Son, who is Christ, claims the middle as something peculiar to Himself, when the series of intellectual things was discussed by Moses under the metaphor of a garden and trees, he describes the tree of life planted in the midst of that garden, which, without doubt, is Christ, who is called the bread of life, the tree of life, and life itself. But it was planted in the middle, so that each person might more easily receive from the fullness of its life according to his capacity. Hence also, when the fullness of time came, this tree was grafted into the tree of assumed nature in the very center of the world, so that it might distribute its fruits to all around in due proportion: Concerning which grafting, James says: "Receive the engrafted word, which is able to save your souls." And this tree of life, namely the divine person grafted into human nature, is the tree of the knowledge of good and evil: because He alone (as we said elsewhere), being a wayfarer, experienced the good of blessedness and the evil of human passions. Moreover, He is the tree of good and evil, because He, above others, knew how to discern good from evil,
[Marginal note: Isaias.] according to that prophecy of Isaiah: "He shall eat butter and honey, that he may know to refuse the evil, and choose the good." Nor did He only know, but He also taught us to know true goods, which we ought to love, and true evils to be feared and avoided by us. Finally, He is the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, to whom judgment and the knowledge of discerning good and evil were given: Whence, as He Himself testifies in the Gospel, when He comes to the universal judgment, He will place the good on the right, but the evil on the left, standing Himself in the middle, and separating these from those by perpetual segregation. But this tree was therefore forbidden from the beginning, that it should not be touched, or tested, or eaten from, because no one ought to experience or test the law and judgment existing in Him, but to revere and fear, and always have before their eyes, so that we might direct all our actions towards its goal: In which sense we do not doubt that that saying of the living God was spoken: "These words, which I command you today, shall be in your heart: and you shall tell them to your children, and you shall meditate on them sitting in your house, and walking on the way,"

which is found in Dionysius [Marginal note: Diony] and other wise men in seeking what evil is, and whence it draws its origin: To resolve this, indeed, seems to be of the greatest difficulty, since evil is not a being, nor pure nothing, nor any cause, since every cause is something really existing: Nor does it seem to be an effect, because every effect proceeds from a cause, and such a cause is that in operating it always looks to the good: and always does good, although in a free agent imagination often errs, deeming or feigning that to be good which is not good: Nor does it seem how evil can arise from good, with the highest truth proclaiming: A good tree cannot bear bad fruit: And also, because nothing comes from contraries, except as from a starting point, as the Peripatetics [Marginal note: Peripat] are accustomed to say. Therefore, let Manichaeus lie here, who dreamed of two principles, one of good things, and that good, the other of evil things, and that evil: For there cannot be a producing principle unless it is good: Nor can a duality exist unless it draws its origin from a unity: Therefore, there would absolutely be one first principle, from which these two principles would emanate: Nor could God be happy if anything invincible opposed Him. Christ was the best mediator. Chapter VI.
[Decorative initial M] Rightly, therefore, this one, who is central in divine matters, and planted in the midst of paradise like a tree in the middle of a garden, and always maintained a middle position in life, became the true and best mediator between God and man, according to that saying of the apostle: There is one mediator of God [Marginal note: Paul] and men, Christ Jesus: Who is a true mediator for multiple reasons, but especially (as some think) from the flesh and human nature assumed: because of which, participating in both extremes, he was a good medium, a bond, and a glue binding, connecting, and uniting man with God: By which office, because true priests also function, any of them is called a mediator, not indeed the primary, but secondary, and holding the place of the true and primary mediator. He is moreover the best medium and mediator, and as it were a certain channel, through whom from the living and supreme fount flow living waters to us, which he freely offers us in many places: From which one possesses as much of the higher influx as one receives from the fullness of this mediator. Nor finally will a creature be able to return to God, from whom it proceeded, except through this medium, which participates in both extremes.

Through Christ man we ascend to God and the Father. Chapter VII.
[Decorative initial E] Thus, therefore, our Christ here is the middle way and the ladder by which we ascend to God the Father, as he himself openly declares in the Gospel, which is titled according to John, saying: I am the way, no one comes to the Father except through me. Who also showed himself to the ancient patriarch Jacob, in whose house he was to reign, in the figure of a ladder, [Marginal note: John] by which the chosen posterity of the seer would ascend to God: For the lower end of this ladder was fixed on earth, because the soul of the mediator, which was given as the price of human redemption, and prepared the way by which we might ascend to God, was fixed, just like other souls, in the flesh, which divinity itself accompanied: indeed the other end of the ladder, or the supreme summit of Christ the mediator himself, touched heaven, penetrating it even to God the Father, who leaned upon that summit, as if resting in it, and upholding the same, according to that saying of the same Son of God, which no one but he himself would have dared to assert: I am in the Father, and the Father is in me [Marginal note: CHRIST] : And again: The Father dwelling in me, he himself does the works. perfect, and in no way deficient, was a full executor of the new testament: Which testament was promulgated by the Son, and committed to execution: but ordained by the Father, as the Son himself testifies in the Gospel, which is titled according to Luke, saying: Behold, I appoint to you a kingdom, just as my Fa-

Behold therefore from these, and many other places, those things which pertain to the new testament were disposed by the Eternal Father: but committed to execution by the Son: to whom he granted such power, that he could even make a testament. Therefore, Jesus Christ was a testator by the power given to him by the Father: he was also the executor of this better testament, just as Moses was of the former:

But why this new testament is better than
[Marginal note: Paul.] the old, Paul, assigning a reason with the Hebrews, says: Because it is sanctioned by better promises: For in the former testament, this lower land was promised, namely the land of Canaan, flowing with that milk and honey, about which it has often been said. But in the second, the land which is the flesh, and the tabernacle of the soul, and the divinity of the Messiah, was promised and given, from which flowed more perfect milk and honey than from the land of Canaan: For from his very fleshly body, that wisdom was communicated to us, which none of the wise of this age had known before, and that mellifluous taste was given to the human race, so that an innumerable multitude of men and women, enticed by that sweetness, exposed body and soul to various and most atrocious kinds of death: Which they could by no means have suffered with such alacrity, unless strengthened and anointed by the sweetness of honey flowing from the divinity through the earthly flesh and humanity of Christ.

Finally, that land of the living was promised, as the testator himself clearly promises in the Gos-
[Marginal note: CHRIST.] pel, which is titled according to Matthew, saying: Blessed are the meek, for they shall inherit the earth. Again, in the former testament, length of life was frequently promised upon that lo-
[Marginal note: Deut.] wer land, and especially in that place where it is said in Deuteronomy: Keep the commandments of the Lord, and the ceremonies, and the judgments, that you may live, and that he may multiply you, and bless you in the land which you are entering to possess. For he is your life, and the length of your days: that you may dwell in the land for which the Lord swore to your Fathers: But in the new testament, a heavenly, divine, and eternal life is promised.

Also, in the former testament, elemental rain, fertility of the earth, abundance of fruits, and finally every favor and abundance of temporal things were promised: But in the new, the pastures of the better man are promised, to be taken within and without, namely in both natures of Christ. Also promised was a generous influx of fruits, and of all heavenly goods, namely graces, charisms, and all divine things. Again, in the former testament, peace that would soon be lost was promised, and victory over human enemies, Assyrians, Philistines, Moab, Ammon, Amalek, and the like:

But in the new testament eternal peace is promised, to be preserved by an everlasting covenant, just as the testator said at his departure: "My peace I give to you, my peace I re- [Marginal note: CHRIST.] linquish to you:" certainly not that which the world is accustomed to give, but a better one, both with God and with angels, which the world itself cannot give: But we can by no means attain this, unless a perfect victory has first been achieved: which also (as Paul testifies) we obtain through our sole mediator: in which victory and peace [Marginal note: Paul.] we obtain every good.

Digression concerning the war declared against those peoples by the ancient Fathers. Chapter IX.

[Large decorative initial E] AND because we have touched upon the perpetual war entrusted to the ancient fathers against the Assyrians, Philistines, and other peoples recently named, we have by no means thought it right to omit an unexplained matter, because all other things happened to those fathers in figure (or symbolically). We have not, however, considered this unimportant, especially because of two points touched upon in the declaration of that war, which seem by no means fitting for the people of God, and even less for God himself: One of these is, because a perpetual war was commanded, and even to the utter destruction of the enemies, and of all things which they possessed. The other, because it is declared that there is perpetual war between God and these enemies themselves.

Concerning the former, there is God's precept in Deuteronomy against Amalek in these words: "Remember what Amalek did to you on the way, when you came out of Egypt, [Marginal note: Deut.] how he attacked the rear of your army, those who were weary and lagging, when you were exhausted by hunger and labor, and he did not fear God: Therefore, when the Lord your God has given you rest, you shall blot out his name from under heaven." Since this was not fully done, therefore it is again commanded to Saul, that he should destroy Amalek himself, and all that was his, even to the smallest animals, and all his household goods, as we read in the first book of Kings. Concerning the [Marginal note: Book of Kings.] latter, however, we have in Exodus, how the hand upon the throne of God is said to fight against Amalek himself from generation to generation: These, he says, A- [Marginal note: Exodus.] malekites together with Assyrians, Philistines, Moabites, and Ammonites, indicate certain powers of darkness, against which a most fierce war has been declared for us, and perpetual enmities have been set, as it is said in Genesis: "I will put enmities between you and the seed of the woman," because that ancient serpent (of whom Amalek was a member and [Marginal note: Genesis.] a certain power) presumed to oppose the first man, and consequently his posterity proceeding to the true land of promise, and a place truly and not figuratively destined, just as here, following a father and leader, he presumed to oppose the people going to a figurative place. Hence, against both, a perpetual war has been declared without any peace or truces, and against all that is theirs, because all those things are an impediment to us striving for our homeland. Hence, we who are to fight for Christ vow to renounce the devil, the world, and

Hence the Church forbade anyone to say Hallelujah during the time of penance, before a person was fully
purified: which, interpreted, means, 'Praise Jah.'
And this those ancient and good Fathers learned from David, full of God, who never
wanted to sing Hallelujah unless he had first removed, through many psalms, whatever
[Marginal note: David.] impediments there were to this most celebrated praise:
Hence, at the end of the one hundred third psalm,

Father fights upon the seat of divinity for Adonai, that is, Christ, and our
mediator, against Amalek, namely the diabolical power, until hostile
death is utterly destroyed and swallowed up in the victory given by God to Christ
the head and His members. It is not surprising, therefore, if such a dire and perpetual
war has been declared against us against this Amalek and peoples similar to him: And if
God is said to continually wage war against them, not indeed for Himself, but granting
us victory through JESUS Christ our Lord: From which we conclude
that He is also the mediator of the victory to be obtained by us.

Whether we need a means to come to this Christ the mediator. Chapter X.

[Decorative initial E]
And since it can be questioned whether another means is necessary for us, through
which we may come to this mediator: Concerning this, briefly explaining myself,
I say that there is no mediator of a mediator, lest we proceed to
infinity, but two means, or prior dispositions, are rightly required,
through which we may receive him and be united to him: Of these, one
emanates from above, namely, the election of divine clemency and piety, placing
us among the sheep that had perished from the true house of Israel, for whose redemption he
came: The other is, that we labor faithfully with the talents entrusted to us, so that that election
may be effective in us, according to the purpose of the chooser, and that we follow the footsteps
of the mediator himself, who said: "I have given you an example, that just as I have
done, so also you may do:" Who again exhorts and invites us to follow him, [Marginal note: CHRIST.]
saying: "Whoever follows me does not walk in darkness, but will have the light of life:"
that light indeed, which illuminates every person, provided that no one, enveloped in the dark-
ness of sins, voluntarily refuses that light, through which, without any
other means, divine election standing firm, we can be united with the mediator, and receive,
according to our capacity, all things which we have explained in this canticle are to be communicated
from the super-mundane source to all members of the Christian body through the head
and our mediator Christ: from whose fullness each one receives a part suitable to himself.

**OF THE SECOND CANTICLE**

**Proem to the Third and Newest Canticle.**

[Decorative initial C]INCE we have now completed two canticles, of which the first, and ancient one, pertains to the harmony of the greater world with the lesser, and the archetype; the second, new one, concerning the agreement of all members with Christ the head, has been dealt with; it remains that we approach the newest canticle, by which we may complete the harmonious progress and state of the lesser world, for whose sake all things were made, into its due end. Which we consider all the more pleasing to the Supreme Prince, the more accurately it has fashioned man himself, beyond the other things we have already discussed. Concerning which canticle (if I am not mistaken) the Prophet, imbued with full light to understand all things, prophesied, when he said: God, I will sing a new song to you. Indeed, I will sing of man, who is God's newest work, to be brought into harmony with the Creator, through the observance of the law and the ten precepts, which are indicated by the ten-stringed psaltery on which the Prophet played.
[Marginal note: David.]
Since the sacrament of these precepts is entirely contained in the evangelical cithara, and the praise of both is rendered by a well-strung body, and a harmonious spirit, and a well-singing soul, therefore he sings in another hymn: Rejoice, O well-strung men, in God our helper, from whom comes all perfect symphony and praise. Shout for joy to the God of Jacob, you who have overcome and trampled all impediments to due praise.
[Marginal note: The same.]
Take up a psalm, by which you may praise God with mind and soul, and give in His praise a well-composed drum of the body, and then you will take up the joyful psaltery with the cithara. For the most joyful psaltery of the law is taken up when it is perfected in the evangelical cithara, in which (as is clear to one who understands well) even the smallest 'yod' and the tiniest 'tittle' of the law itself is fulfilled. For it contains all its sacraments.

And then harmonious songs are rendered, when with the well-strung instruments of body, spirit, and soul, we render to God, to the best of our ability, due praises and harmonious works. But we render fuller songs when, having overcome and subdued our enemies, we arrive at the true praises of Yah (יה), as the prophet teaches in the first hundred and three psalms, when he says: Let sinners vanish from the earth and the wicked, so that they are no more; bless the Lord, O my soul, Hallelujah, that is, praise Yah.
[Marginal note: The same.]
Which no one can do unless enemies are put to flight, as we are taught in the aforementioned psalms. But we shall render the most perfect and fullest songs (God willing) when we praise Him in the highest together with the angels, resounding in that choir of the blessed, not only with the tongue, but with spirit, soul, body, and all members, to the praise of the Creator, to whom all things owe glory and honor forever. And this we shall accomplish with the diapasonic consonance of eight tones, just as we have done in the two preceding canticles.

delight to those who behold it. For all those measurements are divided by multiple, or superparticular, or mixed proportions: from which always results harmony, either simple or compound. For a decuple proportion makes a triple octave and a fifth. An octuple [makes] a triple octave. A quadruple, a double octave; a sexcuple, a double octave and a fifth. A triple, an octave and a fifth. And in a similar way all the commensurations of other members are proportioned and consonant: and what is greater, they are most congruent with the members of the world, with the joints of the heavens, and with the measurements of the archetype, which is supreme.
